nodes.title: html-portfolio [main, claude/serene-franklin-9w7f1v]: Meera/Maya Hinglish AI companion (chat, Gemini Live voice, screen-watch, memory graph, games, Capacitor APK) built on top of a reusable, heavily measured "RelationalOS" layer: one prompt compiler, persona modules, a surface contract, predicate safety, a turn trace, a failure ladder and a CI-validated context/ memory system. Both branches are identical at 3a921798 (2026-08-25).

Context memory system: graph.json index plus decisions (each with a reversal condition), measurements (n/method/date), rejected and architecture files, validated in both directions by context.mjs --check in CI

Prompt compiler (CORE/TAIL): Single compile() for every lane: byte-stable cacheable CORE plus budgeted TAIL slots with whole-block drop order, rules that must fire appended last (shapelint-enforced), and hashCore/byte-identity fixtures that protect the prefix cache
Prompt-budget gate: Fails the build if a compiled prompt would be silently truncated; runs fixtures through the real compiler and checks manifest arithmetic
AgentModule persona registry: Persona as an injected module or CharacterSheet; a second agent is a registry row (Kabir passes 412/412 invariants)

Honesty output gate: Predicate on output bytes: an identifier not present in the input counts as invented (provenance allowlist that keeps helplines by mechanism), plus receipt and presupposition detectors and content-preservation controls
Surface adapter contract: Channels implement verify/parse/send/render only; identity, recall, compile, gate and logging are shared; a single fail-closed gatedReply site is asserted structurally
Person x Agent x Surface tenancy: Relationship keyed by (agent_id, person_id); vy_surface_identity has no agent_id; agent-scope WHERE predicate applied before ranking
Structural disclosure: Privacy as a SQL WHERE clause over episode participants, with withdraw-not-delete; 0 leaks in 31,122 checks
Upstream failure ladder: One classifier (quota / deterministic / transient), same-key retry, wall-clock deadline, family cooling and a two-phase fuse; driven by a fake-clock eval
Azure OpenAI v1 lane: Azure Foundry chat/vision last-resort lane with deployment defaults; skips cleanly when unconfigured; embeddings helper
Turn trace: Seven-leg per-turn spine plus append-only legs; client is the only writer; converging upserts; stores references and hashes, never content; zero added SQL on the reply path

Episodic memory and consolidation: Episodes as citation ground truth, index-only citations, 5% second-family entailment audit that halts the run, contradictions as new rows, hard-delete forget with suppression, nightly finalize
Semantic recall on Neon: halfvec(1536) person-filtered exact scan (40ms p50) run concurrently with keyword recall
Client-side voice floor: Hold ring, echo coefficient, LISTEN/BARGE bars, silence heartbeat, stuck-endpoint watchdog, goAway rotation; the client owns barge-in decisions
Echosim audio-floor simulator: Transpiles the real liveCall.ts standalone and drives it through a room impulse response; 80-call floor table plus stucksim and rotatesim
Voice identity guard and spoken-text sanitiser: Asserts every lane names the same voice and model; sanitiser with mustSay content-preservation tests
Lifecycle matrix as code: Events x contexts grid where each cell names its carrier and a reason; a declared-but-dead direct cell fails the build
verify-release and workflow lint: One command runs all gates and prints failures together; --live probes are opt-in; lints illegal contexts in job-level if:; CI config stub
Scene wake detector: Pure geometry over a 32x32 luma grid; wakes on the hold not the change; no taste in code
Capacitor OTA updater: Web bundle zip with external sha256 manifest; update origin pinned in the APK
Judge qualification method: Both-orders judging, test-retest ceiling, position-bias detection, swap-test pre-registration

html-portfolio [claude/ai-companion-app-rkt1lv, claude/zen-keller-dydb02, codex/meera-forget-integrity-oct09]: The newest Meera/Maya companion line: about 38 commits on top of main (which already holds the world layer, the RelationalOS split and the resilience ladder). It adds the 2026-08-25 hardening wave, the Oct-04 password gate and forget-requires-asking incident fixes, plus two lines that diverge: a partial-forget episode-integrity fix (codex branch) and maya.vyakti.ai preview tags (claude branches).

Upstream failure ladder + lane order: A single classifier sorts upstream failures into quota, transient, deterministic or empty_200. Transient failures get a same-key retry with jittered backoff and a hard wall-clock deadline. Lane order lives in visible constants, and with the flag off the original frozen array is returned by identity.

Explicit prompt-cache manager: Explicit Google cachedContents keyed by a SHA-256 of the core bytes. TTL acts as garbage collection, refreshes are rate-limited, and a dead cache name is recreated before falling back to an uncached call. Live-verified at -77%.

Internals disclosure fence: A deterministic output predicate for three severe disclosure shapes: confirmation, volunteered vendor name, and architecture claim. It allows one re-draft and has documented cases where it must not fire. Offline: 2/2 severe cases caught, 0 false positives across 205 replies.

Loop/repeat fence: A pure function of the transcript that detects topics she over-raises (signal: she uses the word, he does not; no stoplist) and near-duplicates of her own replies (Jaccard 0.8). Allows one re-draft and arms the next turn on streamed lanes.

Behavioral attack battery: 208 attack turns, including Hinglish twins, run through the real compiled prompt. Predicate graders with severity tiers, a cash cap enforced before each call, a --dry mode that makes zero model calls, and gate-shaped exit codes.

Verified-human-intent for destructive LLM actions: userAskedToForget requires a delete-class word from the user in this turn or the 90s burst before it, in Latin or Devanagari script, before honoring the model's [forget] marker. claimsDeletion scrubs any reply line that claims a deletion happened. 44 checks.

Partial-forget episode integrity CTE: One SQL statement that unlinks the surviving raw log rows, inserts content-free provisional wake episodes so the consolidator re-segments them, then deletes the doomed episodes. Passed CI; codex branch only.

Shared-password server gate: An HMAC token derived from the access word(s). Off when the env var is unset; changing the word revokes every token. One client fetch wrapper; an eval asserts the protected and open route lists.

Ops event stream: A server ops event writer that never throws and records only counts, labels and decisions (never text), into meera_diag scope ops. Comes with the lesson that the path is not proven until a row has been read back.

Append-only consent ledger: A DPDP memory-consent table with no update path: the newest row is the current answer, and no column can hold anything a person said. Comes with a warm consent UI and a decline path that closes the memory write gate.

CharacterSheet / Relational Core split: Personas are typed fragment fields interpolated into a character-agnostic core. A byte-identity gate and a residue-leak ratchet pinned at 0 guard the split. A second persona (Kabir) passed 412/412 invariants with zero engine changes.

Single compiler with CORE/TAIL + budget gate: One prompt assembler for every lane. The safety floors sit in a byte-stable, never-truncated core (also the cache unit), and the volatile tail goes last. The budget gate throws instead of truncating silently.
Gated surface adapter: All surfaces (Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord) route replies through one gatedReply call site. A static eval proves no ungated path exists.
context/ memory system: Decisions carry reversal conditions; measurements carry n, method and date; rejections are logged; a graph.json index is validated by scripts/context.mjs --check.
India market and regulatory sweep: 43-source sweep: Indian voice-agent pricing (₹3-65/min), TRAI outbound-AI rules, DPDP timelines, and companion-category ad policy.

html-portfolio [voice-cloning]: Vyakti Replica Lab: a consented self-replica control plane (identity/liveness, private evidence processing, provider-neutral VoiceGenome, Azure Personal Voice + self-hosted Chatterbox, blinded voice curriculum, watermark/C2PA provenance, erasure, spend ledger). It is fully built and passes its offline tests, but nothing has been measured live.

Atomic paid-provider spend ledger: Reserves conservative cost before provider I/O, marks a one-way begin, settles measured usage, and locks ambiguous outcomes as reconcile_required. Covers Foundry tokens, Speech audio seconds and Personal Voice profiles/characters under one grant ceiling.

Provider-neutral voice contract + registry: createVoice/getVoiceStatus/synthesizeStream/deleteVoice interface with fixed 24kHz s16le mono PCM output. The AI disclosure prefix is enforced by the contract, provider refs stay server-only, and fake providers are refused in production.

Azure Personal Voice adapter: Flow is consent resource, then profile, then pinned-base-model SSML synthesis to raw PCM. Operation-Ids are deterministic, deletion is idempotent, WAV input is byte-probed and each call is metered. Mock-tested only because Limited Access was never approved.
Strict WAV/PCM prober: Validates RIFF bounds and format fields, takes duration from the PCM itself, and rejects clipping, DC offset, silence and polyglot tails.
Azure Speech fast-transcription adapter: Metered fast-transcription client (api-version 2025-10-15) aimed at Hinglish, with content-free errors. Tested only against mocked responses.

Queue/lease DAG worker + Container Apps Job: Leased idempotent stages with create-only writes, rehash-on-write and content-free outcome codes. Runs as a scale-to-zero Container Apps Job with ClamAV and ffprobe.

HMAC admission broker in front of scale-to-zero GPU: A CPU broker validates body HMAC, nonce and timestamp before forwarding to a private GPU app, so random traffic cannot wake paid GPU capacity. Images are pinned by digest and Bicep is included.

Voice-evidence GPU service: Runs diarization, two-speaker separation, dual enhancement candidates and two speaker-embedding families. HMAC-authenticated in both directions, with models baked into the image.

Blinded Bradley-Terry active preference curriculum: Picks pairs by Fisher information plus an uncertainty term, applies a repeat penalty, rotates prompts through a deck, and uses a conservative convergence rule (18+ judgments, 6 prompt families).

Held-out qualification gate with Wilson bound: Uses a preregistered 6-prompt x 2-seed holdout with counterbalanced sides. A pass needs a rate of at least 0.75 and a Wilson lower bound above 0.5, and a pass can never auto-promote.

Blinded paired candidate promotion gate: A candidate must improve its target layer, stay non-inferior on the other layers, have zero critical safety failures, keep false memories bounded, and commit to its exact artifact, dataset and baseline.

Leakage-safe feedback dataset compiler + per-layer turn feedback: Builds immutable whole-conversation splits from latest revisions only and forces unsafe sessions into holdout. Feedback is graded separately per layer, and owner corrections are envelope-encrypted and stored as evidence rather than applied as prompt mutations.

Cited claim extraction via Azure Foundry strict output: Masks identifiers, calls Foundry with strict structured output, then re-validates the citations independently. Results are only proposals for review.

Erasure state machine with leased reconciler: Revokes the voice first, then deletes provider copies, source objects and derived models. A leased reconciler retries with exponential backoff and never reaches a terminal give-up state.

Revocation-aware streaming delivery fence + audio protection: Before releasing each signed 240 ms PCM segment, the active capability is checked again. Audio is protected with AudioSeal and C2PA, signed by a non-exportable Key Vault key.

Azure grant allocation plan and model acceptance rule: A $1,829 capped plan inside the $2k grant, with coverage traps (Direct-from-Azure only, no Professional Custom Neural Voice), alert ladder, tagging and expiry discipline, and a rule that a model must win the owned eval set.

Open voice-model landscape with licence verdicts: Sorts open voice models into adopt (VoxCPM2, MOSS-TTS, ZONOS2, OmniVoice, Chatterbox, Qwen3-ASR), route-first, and benchmark-only or reject on licence grounds.

It adds a blind listening bench, a scale-to-zero voice preview, the Mirror Call (backend, tab and reply lane), the Context Locker, a journey/design system, an activity surface and an enrollment queue sweep. Activity surface: Normalises seven async lanes into one job shape. Only real fractions are shown as percentages, an undeployed lane is a named state, polling backs off and stops when nothing is in flight, and an append-only transition log carries a failure-named CHECK.

Processing sweep + capability-absence codes: A cron sweep drains a lease/execute/settle job DAG. Every step always has an adapter; a missing capability is a stub that throws a named code. Jobs are auto-requeued when the capability lands, and the sweep keeps 'blocked on us' separate from 'failed: your bytes'.

Cold-start-as-a-state for scale-to-zero services: Returns 202 warming with a stage, ETA and Retry-After. The pattern is wake then sign. A wake clears the warm belief, and the wake request is never aborted.

Sealed exact-text matched pack + in-studio blind selection: Opaque clip ids, hidden repeats and attention checks, with the model map sealed until ratings lock. Objective scoring runs on opaque ids only, and the reveal uses an RSA-signed report verified by WebCrypto.

Wizard readiness pure function: Readiness is derived from data, with null meaning unknown. At most one active step, unknown blocker codes are still rendered, and the function is fuzzed over 6,912 inputs.

Forget-follows-the-person erasure: Erasure resolves a person's device set (capped, failing closed to the asking device) and wipes every surface, with live negative controls.

context/ project-memory system: Decisions carry reversal conditions; measurements carry n, method and date; rejections are recorded. Includes graph.json with a checker, an AGENTS.md entry door and an append-only session log.
Per-speaker LoRA voice fine-tune: One adapter per expert, composed at load. The adapter travels inside the HMAC-signed body, init uses a private RNG, and a synthesis_commitment hash is recorded.

Perceive/prefetch on stable partial transcripts: Starts classify, the note and speculative replies on the device's stable partial (deltas complete about 0.3 s before VAD stop); the turn adopts them only on a byte-identical fingerprint, else recomputes. Degrades and never fails.

Framed TTS v2 / turn-audio fold + ADPCM + DragonHD streaming: One response carries the turn JSON frame, PCM or IMA-ADPCM (4:1, slow links) frames with sample-exact clause/viseme events, and an end frame. DragonHD SSML streams raw PCM 24 kHz with the voice per character as config, falling back to gpt-4o-mini-tts with the fallback counted. TTS is prewarmed during the DB transaction.

Ack / continuer gate: Uptake echo of the caller's answer token and a non-verbal continuer (hmm/accha/okay) as first sound. It fires only after the distress read, never twice running, never on stop or leave, never with content words, and uses a positive lexical gate with absolute-refusal words. Measured -1.2 s perceived latency.

Duplex engine + cascade barge-in pause-then-decide: Floor manager, EOT with lexical horizon, echo skeleton match across Roman/Devanagari, barge-in duck (local onset duck at about 90 ms, pause, transcript decides), continuer resume, half-duplex mic gating with output-latency tail, and one-turn-at-a-time rule.

Latency harnesses: End-to-end child-stops-to-first-sound with stage breakdown, agent model first-clause bake-off, 429 overflow arm with paired bootstrap 90% CIs, phone-profile start (Playwright CPU x4), region TTS TTFB, long-task probe, cascade latency, realtime TTFA and audio-in VAD arms, WebRTC ephemeral-key probe.
Boot-warm: Builds heavy tables before listen, slices kit normalisation one per event-loop turn, and precompiles Unicode regexes, so no first request after deploy pays 1-1.6 s event-loop blocks.

One certificate gate + producer-scan test: Every server path that can reveal UI calls certifyForTray/certifyModule at the device viewport before reveal. A test scans server/shared source and fails on any new ungated producer; a mutation check proves the test bites.

Rendered-artifact visual QA (forge3 measure): In-Chromium measurement of rendered text px, clipping, overlap and composition fill, including a canvas fillText probe installed via an init script. Runs at named viewports 360/412/1366.

Closed-enum model 'dress' pattern: One fast model call may change presentation only through a strict closed-enum schema. The answer is validated field by field (invalid values dropped, never repaired), with a 1.9 s deadline falling back to a code base. No model string reaches the user.

Forge G1 live personalised fill pipeline: Pipeline: plan (code) → cache (memory → Neon) keyed by canonical-JSON sha256 over versions + model + kit + item + skin → optional enum-only model flavour (≤ 3.5 s) → code build → code gate → mount. scene@1 generative-UI DSL: A zod schema as the single source, emitting JSON Schema and a strict wire schema for Azure structured outputs. Includes an expression language with no eval, a layout pass, lint S1-S7, a goal solver and autofix.

Studio archetype library: Twelve JSON interaction archetypes plus a whiteboard archetype. Each has a params schema, truth rules, string keys, budgets and anti-patterns. The prompt builder puts the rules last, and there is a scripted QA player per archetype.

Forge G2 sandboxed agent-codegen on ACA Jobs: One ACA Job execution per build in a separate untrusted environment, with a per-build blob container and a 2-hour SAS. Signed-session + server-replay grading: The client runs a pure law and records raw act envelopes. A first-committed-act evidence rule writes one evidence row per level.
Economy / dark-pattern lint: Tests that fail on persisted counters, wall clock or RNG in progress code, untraced progress writes and economy vocabulary. Planted violations trip 6/6 rules.

Juice limits module: Game-feel effects capped in one place: hit-stop ≤ 80 ms, shake ≤ 6 px, celebration ≤ 800 ms, ≤ 90 particles. Includes easing set and spring; reduced motion jumps to the end state.

core3d engine contract + stage: three.js stage with DOM labels holding size floors, a DPR-ratchet frame governor, context loss falling back to a 2D twin, an audio bus with voice duck, tiering, and twin-first loading.
Greedy voxel mesher in a Web Worker: Chunk mesher with corner AO; mesh 0.1-0.2 ms p50 off the main thread.

Kaksha / Volt token design system: Scoped themes via .kx[data-klook][data-ktheme], raw hex only in token files, and a one-accent ('volt') law. Chamfer and HUD components, spring motion and a reduced-motion stop. Lint tests ban colour literals and check every token pair at ≥ 5:1 contrast. Legacy tokens are re-pointed through var() only.
Flag-gated redesign parity harness: Proves non-cohort accounts get byte-identical DOM and pictures (72/72) and fetch no new chunks.

Design-direction prototype + lint + judge harness: Self-contained offline HTML prototypes covering 12 states × 2 viewports × 3 languages. A lint checks text px, Devanagari px, target px and contrast, and a judge script compares directions.
Real-capture marketing site pipeline: Landing-page images are re-captured from the real app's dev fixtures, so the site never shows a screen the app does not draw.

Persona talk-gate (simulated user talk share): Gates persona or prompt changes on the simulated user's talk share against a same-harness baseline (10% drop rule).

Voice duplex bake-off + cost-per-minute (Azure meters, ACS PSTN): Five-arm duplex bake-off with phone-speaker echo and a scorer, plus a cost per conversation-minute for enterprise voice calling.

Owner idea 1 (unbiased idea, to be tested): Emotional, relational, extremely human-like conversational voice agents
nodes.triage:
Reframe as human-competent: language lock, turn-taking, backchannels, short replies, safe numbers and binding commitments. That is core for the wedge.

'Emotional/relational' has no outcome evidence:
- In the collections study, AI was not hung up on more within 10 s. The gap came with 21 pp fewer promises, which the paper says only 'may contribute' [l5v].
- AI trails human sellers on sales-process discipline (n=366), and disclosure no longer cuts conversion (n=1,337) [l5v].
- Warmth backfires with angry customers and collides with collections conduct rules [l5].

Measure warmth in a pilot befo

nodes.title: Owner idea 2 (unbiased idea, to be tested): Self-evolving agents that learn from every call (e.g. modify the line where 90/100 dropped)
nodes.triage:
Core in scoped forms:
- per-contact memory, from 1 call;
- line-level drop-off mining: a line that doubles hang-ups is found 67% of the time at 500 calls and 76-94% at 1,000;
- local-metric fix confirmation, ~1,200 calls [l6v].

Not valid as stated:
- '90 of 100 dropped' cannot validate a line: the minimum detectable drop is 13-19 pts at 100 calls per arm [l6].
- Daily-checked K=2 dashboards declare false winners in 52-62% of A/A runs by day 90 [l6v].
- Outcome optimisation needs ~1,000 calls/day per script, and only 22% of insurance buyers can test a +10% lift in month one [l6].

nodes.title: Owner idea 3 (unbiased idea, to be tested): Hyper-personalisation: regional accent/dialect (e.g. Bihari-Hindi mix), per-person memory, cross-source user data
nodes.triage:
Core: regional-language matching and per-contact memory. Memory is parity in India, not a moat [l6].

Later, opt-in only: dialect.
- Employers ask for a dialect in 1 of 828 Hindi-belt postings [l5v].
- Azure has no Hindi-belt dialect TTS [l5].
- Automatic inference fails: a telecom circle is too coarse and language ID cannot separate Bhojpuri from Hindi [l5v].
- The listener panel has not run.

Drop: pooling personal data across sources and tenants. DPDP s.8(2) contracts constrain it and WhatsApp data is barred [l1, l6].

nodes.title: Owner idea 4 (unbiased idea, to be tested): Company context ingested at onboarding
Owner idea 5 (unbiased idea, to be tested): Price under Rs 2/min, components built in-house
nodes.triage:
Rs 2/min is not reachable at the measured quality bar on managed Azure: the floor is Rs 2.1-2.3 and MC p50 is Rs 3.06 at 1M min/month [l2v]. Indian all-in list prices are Rs 3.5-7 [l4av].

So the pricing unit changes (per renewal), not the quality, and Rs 2 becomes a scale-stage COGS target. The only robust <= Rs 2 path is D-lite at Rs 1.16 from ~1.5M min/month, and it is quality-gated.

Build in-house the differentiating layers: compliance router, competence layer, attribution and memory. Do not build commodity ASR or TTS: open ASR fabricates on silence [l7], and self-hosting needs NVAIE lice

nodes.title: VP research round 1: 10 hypothesis lanes + 10 adversarial verifiers + synthesis + critic + founder kit + listener panel (24 agents, ~INR 1,924 Azure est.). Every prediction was at least partly wrong; critic found 4 decision-level problems -> round 2 launched.

Provisional beachhead (round 1): Retail insurance distribution. The buyers are IRDAI-registered retail intermediaries: IMFs (940), retail-focused brokers (out of 874, of which 791 are direct brokers mostly in commercial lines), non-bank corporate agents (out of 689, mostly banks), and the renewal books of PoSP/insurtech platforms such as Turtlemint (550k+ PoSPs). Source [l3, l3v, l4c]. Mode ~1,300 in-reach firms, ~980 of which phone [l3]. — Renewal reminders and lapse revival for motor, health and life policies, each ending in a WhatsApp utility template (Rs 0.115) carrying a payment link and an autopay-mandate option. RBI allows auto-debit without extra authentication up to Rs 1 lakh for insurance premiums [l4cv]. Callback handling and human escalation are included. A renewal or expiry reminder counts as a service call under TCCCPR def (bh)(i) [l1].; Outbound-consented service calls to the intermediary's existing policyholders, plus inbound callbacks. No cold calling. No promotion or cross-sell inside the call: one offer line makes the whole call promotional, so a cross-sell needs a separate 140xx call with consent [l1]. Calls go from tenant-held numbers. These are 1600xx if the IRDAI 1600 mandate (in force since 2026-02-15) covers intermediaries, which is unverified; otherwise A2P-declared 10-digit CLIs [l1].; buyer The founder or principal officer of an IMF or retail broker. At a PoSP platform or non-bank corporate agent, the head of renewals or operations. Reached by founder-led direct sales to the enumerable IRDAI registers (~2,500 firms) [l4c].; pricing Per renewal collected on the due list the AI works, earned in code from the payment record, plus a monthly platform minimum. Incremental saves measured against a 10-20% holdout are reported as the proof of value. Not per minute: the managed cost of goods sold (COGS) of Rs 3.1-5.9/min against Indian list prices of Rs 3.5-7/min leaves no per-minute margin [l2v, l4av]. Under H2's rule, the pricing unit changes, not the quality bar. (Hypothesis to test in interviews:
- Effective yield of Rs 6-8 per AI-connected minute, at or below a human's Rs 6-9 per connected minute [l2v]. Kill below about Rs 6/min-equivalent or Rs 150 per renewal saved [l3].
- Pilot Rs 25-50k/month per renewal book.
- Production about Rs 1.1-1.5 lakh/month for a median modelled buyer: 9,440 calls x ~2 min, both assumptions [calc from l6, l2]. This sits inside the sales-led band of Rs 25k-2L [l4c].
- Billed by invoice, e-NACH or prepay, because card and UPI auto-debit needs extra authentication above Rs 15k [l4cv].). Confidence moderate-low.
nodes.reverse_if: Fewer than 5 of 15 qualified intermediaries run at least 3 renewal telecallers or a renewal desk [l3].; Accepted price is below about Rs 6/min-equivalent or below Rs 150 per renewal saved [l3].; The interviewees' own renewal ratio by line is already 90% or more without calling, or they lose no commission on lapses. This tests whether the pain measured at insurers exists at intermediaries [l3v].; After 60 targeted intermediaries, fewer than 10 take a discovery call or fewer than 3 accept a paid pilot within 10 weeks [l4c].; Counsel finds intermediaries must use 1600xx but cannot obtain it, or that non-1600 service calls are unlawful, and the tenant has no compliant number path [l1].; Our agent misses the battery bar on the elderly and Hinglish personas: clean-turn p50 <= 1.5 s, collisions <= 5%, barge-in handled >= 90%, correct language >= 95% of turns, no loop or drop under babble. nodes.title: Owner product brief: Indian enterprises fire voice agents at their customers for pre-sale (selling, market surveys, outreach) and post-sale (feedback, surveys, customer success); find where the main value shows. v1 = what competitors have, made better: product design, usability, UI/UX and animation, whole user flow, every case handled, more intelligence. Onboard in 30-60 min, any data in, fire an agent, every recording, overview + deep analytics. Buyer selects STT/brain/TTS. v2 (later): memory, personalisation across long/frequent conversations, attribute extraction, self-learning agent (e.g. a drop-off line learned by call 100 changes on call 101), visible recursive improvement.

Owner: when building self-improving agents later, use the fundamentals of google-research/harness2 (recursive harness optimisation).

Owner: wants a deeper version of the teardown task, not a bigger one: first state what a top professional would add, the rawest material, the methods and tools, and what external evidence shows it is right; then rewrite the prompt.

Teardown brief (deeper rewrite): 3 decisions (pre/post-sale first, v1 parity floor, where we are measurably better); 8 deep vendors used as a customer (surface map, time-and-motion task list, PSTN call battery, graded architecture, unit economics, failures, India plumbing, v2 notes) + radar + change watch; Bolna blind-inference calibration; external proof via buyers, listener panel, usability sessions.

REA (morluto/rea, read 2026-10-20 at 90e433d): MCP + CLI reverse-engineering toolkit; relevant targets here: websites (structure, scripts, network), HAR captures, JavaScript/Electron bundles and source maps, Android APKs (JADX), packet summaries (SNI, DNS); disclaimer excludes bypassing auth/bot protection and copying proprietary code.

Harness2 (google-research/harness2, read 2026-10-20 at 1cfe254): recursive agent harnessing with fixed weights; task-level Propose-Probe-Compose over 8 editable components (system prompt, guardrails, memory, tool guidance, subagents, skills, scripts, plugins) plus a persistent improvement harness of lessons; model-backed runs expect Vertex AI.

Owner's v1 (competitor parity, made better on design/usability/case handling/intelligence) meets rejected.2026-10-17.parity-undercut (parity + price undercut is no wedge). Different claim: parity as a floor, UX and case handling as the wedge; Indian complaints are ~70% support/billing/account-UI (RAW-17). Unproven until measured.

nodes.title: Tier assignment: main loop Opus 5.5 (extra-high effort, set by the owner's session). Opus 5.5 subagents for judgment: synthesis, adversarial verification of architecture/decision claims, judge panels, product and system design, anything that becomes a context decision. Sonnet 5.5 for execution: research and teardown lanes (browsing, captures, REA runs), build workstreams, tests. Haiku 5.5 for mechanical work: manifests, format conversion, link and secret scans, simple extraction, inbox JSON shaping.
nodes.rationale: Judgment errors compound into the graph and the product, so they get the strongest model; bulk execution is checked downstream by Opus verifiers, so it can run on a cheaper tier.
nodes.reverse_if: Opus verifiers refute or downgrade a materially larger share of Sonnet-lane claims than of Opus-lane claims on comparable work, or usage limits bind on a tier (move work down, never skip verification).

nodes.title: Owner: choose the model (and effort) per use case, by how much strength, intelligence and effort the task requires.
nodes.quote: choose the model depending on the use case and how much strength and intelligence and efforts the usecase will require

nodes.title: Per-task model and effort selection. Judge each task on five things: stakes (does the output become a decision, a graph node, product code or something the owner acts on), ambiguity/novelty, depth of reasoning, whether a stronger agent verifies it downstream, and volume. Default ladder: Opus 5.5 max/xhigh for product and system design, final synthesis, adversarial verification of decision-critical claims, security-sensitive code, judge panels; Opus 5.5 high for core build workstreams (voice runtime, data model), hard debugging, inference from ambiguous evidence (e.g. architecture from captures); Sonnet 5.5 high/medium for standard research lanes, feature code from a clear spec with tests, UI from a design; Sonnet 5.5 low or Haiku 5.5 medium for extraction, formatting, fixtures, synthetic data; Haiku 5.5 low for manifests, secret and link scans, inventories. Escalate: a task that fails verification or proves harder reruns one tier up. Never downgrade verification of a decision-critical claim.
nodes.rationale: Owner directive; cost and limits are spent where judgment matters, and cheap tiers are safe only where a stronger agent checks the result.
nodes.reverse_if: Measured verifier refutation rates show a tier under-performing for a task class (move that class up), or a tier's limits bind (move work down a tier, never drop verification).

nodes.title: Every agent runs Opus 5.5: the main loop at extra-high (owner sets via /effort xhigh), and every workflow agent and subagent with model 'opus' and effort 'xhigh'. Sonnet and Haiku are not used. Supersedes the per-task model ladder. The two runs already in flight (wf_560edf6c-5d6, wf_1e4d0167-0c8) finish on the models they started with; every new workflow and subagent from this point uses Opus 5.5 xhigh.
nodes.rationale: Owner directive: frontier product, frontier models throughout.
nodes.reverse_if: Opus usage limits stall in-flight work (the owner then decides whether to allow a lower tier for bulk mechanical steps); never drop verification.

nodes.title: Owner clarification (correcting a misreading): Opus 5.5 at extra-high is for the main chat only. Workflows, subagents and parallel agents get the model and effort the use case needs, by how much strength, intelligence and effort it requires.
nodes.quote: opus 5.5 extra high in this main chat rest places for workflows and sub and parallel agents choose the model depending on the usecase
nodes.rationale_owner: A mixture of models and efforts gives better performance at lower tokens; invest more where great intelligence is needed.

nodes.title: Owner judged the first authorized-surface run under-powered and asked for a restart on Opus 5.5 (Sonnet 5.5 at least if Opus errors). Stopped wf_1e4d0167-0c8 (nothing had finished) and relaunched as wf_b9977e22-228 with no model override, so every agent inherits the session model claude-opus-5-5; effort xhigh for the Bolna ground-truth lane and the synthesis, high for the four vendor API/SDK lanes; any agent that dies on a terminal error reruns once on Sonnet 5.5 (labelled :sonnet-fallback).
nodes.rationale: Owner instruction for this run; inheriting the session model is the most reliable way to pin Opus 5.5, and the fallback keeps a lane from silently disappearing.
nodes.reverse_if: Fallback labels show Opus 5.5 failing systematically (then run the lanes on Sonnet 5.5 deliberately), or the owner redirects.

nodes.title: Authorized account phase relaunched as wf_36b25033-85c with mixed tiers per the ladder: Opus 5.5 (inherited session model) at xhigh for the Bolna ground-truth lane and the cross-vendor synthesis; Sonnet 5.5 at high for the four standard vendor API/SDK lanes (Vapi, Retell, ElevenLabs, Sarvam), which the Opus synthesis cross-checks. Each agent that dies on a terminal error reruns once on the other tier (label :fallback-opus or :fallback-sonnet). Restart cost: a few minutes of in-flight Bolna work; nothing had completed.
nodes.rationale: Owner directive: a mix of models and efforts gives better performance per token; invest the strongest model where intelligence matters most.
nodes.reverse_if: The synthesis finds the Sonnet lanes' claims materially weaker or wrong (rerun those lanes on Opus 5.5), or fallbacks fire systematically on one tier.

nodes.title: Owner: finish the research, report when all of it is done, and then the owner and agent decide together what product to build and what it will be like.
nodes.quote: continue with the research and when all of its done let me know we will decide what product to build

nodes.title: Which product to build and what it is like (segment and first jobs, v1 scope and parity floor, where VP wins, stack defaults, pricing), decided jointly once the research completes.
nodes.closes_when: Both teardown runs (public wf_560edf6c-5d6, authorized account phase wf_36b25033-85c) finish, a consolidated decision brief is written across all research (2026-10-17 rounds, voice lab, teardown, terms, regulation), and the owner decides.

nodes.title: Owner clarification of intent: the research exists to understand each competitor's product end to end so VP can be better than any of them in every way, while also carrying VP's own extra features (emotional, relational, human-sounding voice; memory and personalisation; later self-learning). Pre-sale vs post-sale was over-weighted; it is an input, not the organising question.
nodes.quote: the intent was to understand ... these product end to end so that we can make a better one then any of them, a product which is better in everyway while having the extra features we are offering

nodes.title: The consolidated decision brief is a product blueprint, organised by product dimension rather than by segment: onboarding, agent builder, conversation and voice quality, telephony, campaigns and data import, compliance handling, analytics and recordings, integrations, the LLM-native setup experience, pricing, reliability and support. For each: how the best competitor does it, where each falls short (evidence-graded), VP's better design, and where VP's own features (emotional voice, memory, personalisation, self-learning later) sit on top. Pre-sale vs post-sale moves to a go-to-market section. The running workflows are not restarted; their outputs feed the blueprint.
nodes.rationale: Owner directive; organising by dimension makes 'better in every way' checkable item by item.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner asks for a different organising frame.

nodes.title: Bolna account-phase teardown: open-source engine read at HEAD bc59921 (43,962 source lines) plus our own API key (57 requests, one synthetic agent created/read/patched/put/deleted, no calls, spend 0, wallet 500.0 before and after). 57 graded claims (49 observed, 4 inferred, 3 vendor-claimed, 1 unknown) covering data model, endpoint surface, call lifecycle, turn-taking, webhooks, metering, config knobs and India gaps. OpenAPI rebuilt from 128 doc-page fragments (96 paths, 183 schemas).

Black-box teardown method calibrated on Bolna: blind architecture inferences scored against the code hit 0.85 (14 TRUE, 6 PARTLY, 0 FALSE), Brier 0.086, against a mean stated confidence of 0.69; it missed every timing constant and turn-taking policy that only the code shows.
nodes.n: 20 checkable blind inferences with contamination none or possible (18 none-only: hit 0.86, Brier 0.093); 4 contaminated rows excluded
nodes.method: Pre-registered rule from research/2026-10-20/teardown/bolna/blind-inferences.json: TRUE/PARTLY/FALSE per row against bolna-ai/bolna @bc59921, hit = (TRUE + 0.5 PARTLY)/n, Brier over stated confidence; verdicts by reading the cited files, 2026-10-20

nodes.title: Inference from code and our API defaults: Bolna's default cascade cannot start a reply sooner than about 1.4 s after the caller's last word from turn 2 on, because 500 ms STT endpointing is followed by a fixed 900 ms incremental_delay audio hold measured from the final; LLM and TTS run inside the hold, transport and 100-200 ms frame buffering add on top. Not yet measured on a call.

Observed in Bolna's code: while the agent speaks, a final transcript of N words or fewer (default N=1) that is not on the English-only exact-match stop list is discarded, so 'nahi', 'haan', 'ruko', 'bas' never reach the LLM; everything said while the welcome plays is dropped (voicemail evidence only); a Hindi agent's check-in defaults to the English 'Hey, are you still there'.

Observed via our API: creating an agent makes Bolna generate two LLM-judge dispositions within about 25 s, 'Call Success' and 'Call Completion' (gpt-4.1-mini, success/failure/unsure), rewritten from the agent's own prompt and Hinglish-aware ('dekhta hoon', 'baad mein' = not success). They are free to the customer, hidden from the dispositions list endpoints and deleted with the agent. Bolna already ships LLM-native outcome analytics by default.

Observed via our API: Bolna's stored agent defaults contradict its API docs (words to interrupt 1 vs 2, incremental_delay 900 vs 400 ms, hangup_after_silence 20 vs 10 s, TTS stream false and 40-char buffer vs true and 250); an unknown field is accepted with 201 and dropped; documented semantic 'routes' are accepted and not persisted; the executions filter shows an undocumented 'prepared' status. Developer-surface gap VP can beat with a tested, spec-first API.

Observed in Bolna's code: mid-call language switching keeps one pre-warmed STT socket per language, runs an unbiased Sarvam saaras:v3 language-ID stream beside the locked live ASR, and asks a dedicated Switch LLM (default Claude Haiku 4.5) to judge the matrix language under about 15 Indic rules before swapping STT, TTS and prompt with a handoff clip. This is the strongest part of the stack and the bar for VP's Hinglish handling; it is still a whole-stack swap, not one code-mixed register.

Observed in Bolna's code: the only production failover is for the LLM, where Azure OpenAI turns on a provisioned deployment are re-issued on a pay-as-you-go overflow deployment on 429/5xx or a stream that drops before any token (retries off when overflow exists, overflow turns metered separately). STT/TTS have reconnects only, the provider circuit breaker runs in shadow, telephony is single-provider per agent.

Observed (API schema + node catalogue): Bolna is call-centric with no contact, consent or memory object, and runs two overlapping outbound systems: batches (CSV, only valid/total counts) and workflow campaigns (row-level failure codes, corrective re-upload, +91 default, de-dup by reference_id not phone, funnel report, 9 node types incl. AiSensy WhatsApp). The only cross-call state is a workflow execution's state.*.

Does Bolna's live behaviour match what its code predicts? The call battery must add: reply gap vs the inferred 1.4 s floor (P09a), short Hindi interjections ('nahi', 'haan', 'ruko', 'bas') spoken over agent speech, caller speech over the welcome, Hindi and regional operator messages for voicemail (P06a), language hold under Hinglish (P11a/b), and a dashboard-created agent's stored defaults vs the API defaults.
nodes.closes_when: Battery run on our verified Plivo number with stereo recordings, n >= 30 turns, scored per item; plus GET /v2/agent readback of one dashboard-created agent.

nodes.title: Competitor platforms run their own LLMs over whatever prompt we store: Bolna rewrote our synthetic agent prompt into two judge questions within 25 s of creation. Putting VP's proprietary persona brief v2, agenda ledger or any real customer data into a competitor account would hand it to their pipelines.
nodes.mitigation: Store only the synthetic standard battery brief and fictional data in vendor accounts; never paste VP's own prompts or customer data; opt out of data use where a vendor offers it before the first call; delete test agents after each session.

nodes.title: Reconstructed Bolna OpenAPI 3.1 spec (96 paths, 183 schemas, merged from 128 public doc-page fragments, 0 conflicts) plus an endpoint table with params and response codes.
nodes.value: Lets the call-battery phase script Bolna calls, batches and webhooks without re-reading 156 doc pages; a template for the same merge on any Mintlify-documented vendor.
nodes.effort: done; regenerate by re-fetching the docs pages and re-running the merge (about 3 minutes)

nodes.title: ElevenLabs Agents authorized-surface phase: 54 graded claims (50 observed, 3 inferred, 1 unknown) from about 110 authorized requests with our free-tier key at about 1 per second, the live OpenAPI (420 operations, 64 exercised), five published packages read without installing (JS SDK, Python SDK, client, types, CLI; plus react) and one REA run on the client SDK dist. No call, number, batch, simulation, test run or webhook. Synthetic probe objects were created, read back and deleted (one environment variable cannot be deleted).

ElevenLabs new-agent defaults differ from its own OpenAPI defaults, and the API ignores typos. A freshly created agent comes back with LLM deepseek-v41-flash (schema: gemini-2.5-flash), speculative_turn true (schema: false), bursting on (excess calls at double price), a 180 s call queue, sentiment and topic analysis on, retention -1 and a US-English default voice (Eric, not verified for Hindi) that the API accepts on a language=hi agent. Unknown properties are dropped with a 200 and still commit a new version. Defaults, not the spec, decide what a buyer gets.

ElevenLabs prices LLM pass-through at USD 0.0054 per minute for gemini-2.5-flash and USD 0.0130 for its server-default deepseek-v41-flash (4,000-character prompt, 5.27 agent messages per minute implied), so the default costs 2.4x the cheaper model: about INR 1.23 against INR 0.51 per minute at FX 95. gpt-5.4-mini is USD 0.0129, claude-sonnet-5 USD 0.0372, gpt-4 USD 0.48; a 12,000-character prompt with 20 pages and RAG multiplies cost about 7.5x.
nodes.n: 111 LLM rows returned per calculator call; 2 calls (4k-character prompt no RAG; 12k-character prompt, 20 pages, RAG)
nodes.method: POST /v1/convai/llm-usage/calculate with our key on 2026-10-20 (free calculator, no call placed); INR conversion at FX 95 is our assumption from the 2026-10-18 cost model

nodes.title: Size of ElevenLabs' agent configuration surface as read back from one new agent: 313 non-widget leaf settings (179 with schema descriptions), 65 per-agent permission strings, 111 selectable LLMs (54 with reasoning-effort levels, 43 deprecated or in warning), 11 TTS models (94 languages on the v4 family), 72 call-start override languages, 26 WebSocket error types, 27 conversation-initiation sources, 40 conversation-list filters, 420 API operations of which 200 are agents/speech-engine. Use as the size to beat for a simpler surface, not a target to copy.
nodes.n: 1 agent read-back (313 leaves) plus counts from the live OpenAPI and GET /llm/list, 2026-10-20
nodes.method: flatten the GET /v1/convai/agents/{id} JSON and join with the OpenAPI schema (research/.../code/derive_knobs.py, derive_surface.py); counts of enum members and operations from the spec

nodes.title: ElevenLabs has an agent-level hinglish_mode flag (mixes English into Hindi, Malayalam, Telugu or Kannada replies; default false) that appears in the OpenAPI and the agent read-back but in none of its 258 saved docs pages. The server persists it even on a language=en agent, so it is not cross-checked, and nothing says what it changes in prompt, ASR or TTS. This is the nearest thing a competitor ships to VP's core idea, and it is a boolean. Its audible effect is untested.

ElevenLabs user memory exists but is gated by a workspace flag. Enabling platform_settings.privacy.user_memory returned 403 "User memories are not available for this workspace"; the knob has scale minimal|balanced|maximum, the workspace has user_memory.retention_days, permissions include agent_view_memories and agent_edit_memories, and the agent reserves a memory_entry_search tool slot that cannot be set through the public schema. Recall by user_id across calls is coming from the leader; how memory is written (facts, summaries, preferences) is unknown.

Reusable reading: ElevenLabs' typed call-event taxonomy (about 40 event types over one socket) from the published @elevenlabs/types 0.25.0, including contextual_update (push text into context without forcing a reply), user_activity, tentative_user_transcript, conversation_history with a persistent_session_token for resume, context_usage, ping with ping_ms, vad_score, guardrail_triggered and 26 error types. A checklist for VP's own event schema, to be re-expressed in our own words, not copied.
nodes.value: Shortcut to a complete list of events a web or phone client of a voice agent must handle, including resume, mid-call context injection and error taxonomy.
nodes.effort: 1 day to turn into a VP event-schema spec

nodes.title: Proposed additions to the v1 parity floor from ElevenLabs' live API (on top of the Vapi list in decision.2026-10-20.acct-vapi-parity-floor-items): an agent version on every write with branch, merge proposal and percentage traffic deployments; three kinds of agent test (response, tool call, simulated persona with up to 30 success conditions and up to 50 turns); post-call evaluation criteria and typed data-collection fields stored on the call; per-turn named latency timers, tool calls and interruption flags in the transcript; a call-result enum and termination reason with a provider error object; fine-grained per-agent permissions; a CLI that pulls and pushes agents as files; pre-call personalisation hook and post-call signed webhooks.
nodes.rationale: All exist in the live API of the funded leader (claims AP-EL-09 to AP-EL-14, AP-EL-26 to AP-EL-28, AP-EL-37, AP-EL-38) and are the baseline a developer or ops buyer compares us with. They are cheap next to the Indian-operator layer and do not differentiate by themselves.
nodes.reverse_if: Buyer interviews (10-15 operations leads) show Indian enterprise users never use branching, simulated tests or webhooks, or a competitor with fewer objects wins the same configure-and-fix tasks in usability sessions.

nodes.title: Proposed places to beat ElevenLabs that its API makes visible: (1) the Indian operator layer is absent from the batch and call objects (no calling window, DND/NCPR scrub, consent or suppression field, no India-specific failure reason); (2) safe defaults: reject unknown fields, cross-check voice against language, show the model actually in effect per call and never reroute silently, retention and redaction chosen at onboarding, bursting off until the buyer opts in; (3) a first-class contact/lead object (ElevenLabs has only a user_id string); (4) dependency-clean deletion; (5) a Hinglish switch that is measured and documented, not a boolean.
nodes.rationale: Each gap is observed in the live API and docs (claims AP-EL-12, AP-EL-13, AP-EL-18 to AP-EL-20, AP-EL-26, AP-EL-27, AP-EL-33, AP-EL-47). They fit the measured pain areas (usability, support, billing) in the 459 coded Indian complaints, and the owner wants better design, usability and case handling.
nodes.reverse_if: A later ElevenLabs release ships the campaigns product with windows, retries and suppression (its dashboard bundle already carries those routes), or buyer interviews rank any of these below price and voice quality.

nodes.title: ElevenLabs LLM deprecation can reroute traffic to a replacement model without the buyer editing the agent (warning 90 days, fallback from 60 days at 25% of traffic, complete at 20 days). A competitor or a supplier doing this to VP would change voice behaviour under a fixed agent version, and a VP test filed under one model may not have run on it (inference from the fields, no live fallback seen).
nodes.mitigation: VP pins every model by dated id, records the model actually used on each call, gates any replacement behind the owner and keeps the no-mid-test-swap rule (directive.2026-10-20.no-midcall-swap).

nodes.title: Rejected: using the ElevenLabs API key to read or manage workspace API keys, billing and seats.
nodes.tried: GET /v1/workspace/api-keys with our xi-api-key; also tried DELETE on an environment variable and DELETE of a tool after its agent was deleted.
nodes.broke: Key listing answered 401 "Neither authorization header nor xi-api-key received" although the key was sent, environment variables have no DELETE route (405), and the tool and KB document stayed "in use by Unknown / Main" (409) until force=true. Key management, billing and seats need a dashboard login; cleanup of probes is partly impossible.

nodes.title: ElevenLabs behaviours the API names but only a call can settle: what hinglish_mode changes, whether a Hindi agent on the default English voice is audibly wrong, what speculative_turn costs in initiated-versus-irreversible LLM generations, whether a live model fallback is visible in the call record, how the bring-your-own-brain speech engine behaves, whether the hidden outbound-campaigns product is enabled on a new workspace, the real handset reply gap with default turn settings, and API rate limits.
nodes.closes_when: The call-battery phase places at least 30 clean turns per configuration (default Hindi agent, voice-swapped Hindi agent, hinglish_mode on and off) on our own verified numbers with a billable plan, and a dashboard-login pass confirms which of the unpublished product areas are visible.

nodes.title: Should VP offer a speech-engine style interface (we run speech, turn-taking and telephony; the customer or we run the brain over a WebSocket)? ElevenLabs ships exactly this (POST /v1/speech-engine with a ws_url and a cascade timeout). It would let VP's Hinglish brain and later memory ride other voice stacks, and it would let competitors put a brain on ElevenLabs' voices.
nodes.closes_when: Buyer interviews show whether Indian enterprises already own a brain (CRM or LLM layer) they want to keep, and the architecture review shows the turn-taking floor holds with a remote brain over India-region links.

nodes.title: Retell authorized-surface phase: 55 graded claims (51 observed, 4 inferred) from about 100 authorized API requests with our own key (one org, vp-teardown), the live OpenAPI, the published retell-sdk (npm and PyPI 6.2.8), the MCP server and web client SDK, and one REA run on the web client SDK. No call, number, batch, chat, knowledge base or test run; probe objects deleted except one synthetic agent and engine.

Retell publishes its whole API: the TypeScript SDK 6.2.8 has 109 method+path operations, the live OpenAPI (revision 2026-10-19-becf7f8, byte-identical to the public-phase copy) has the same 109, no SDK-only routes. Of 38 GET operations swept, 36 answer to an API key and 2 CSV-import routes answer 401 Invalid JWT (dashboard login only). No billing, balance, spend-cap, member or analytics-aggregate route exists.
nodes.n: 109 SDK ops vs 109 OpenAPI ops; 38 GET operations called once each with invalid probe ids
nodes.method: script over src/resources of the extracted npm package compared with the OpenAPI operation list; GET sweep at about 1 request per 1.2 s (limit is 30 to 100 per 10 s) with our API key on 2026-10-20

nodes.title: Retell India depth in its own catalogue: 6 India locales of 63 (en-IN, hi-IN, kn-IN, mr-IN, ta-IN, ur-IN; te-IN rejected by the live validator); 6 of 300 voices have accent Indian, none labelled Hindi; Hindi voices exist only via community search; pronunciation alphabets are ipa, cmu, pinyin, jyutping; the PII categories include no Indian ID type (aadhaar rejected).
nodes.n: 1 voice list (300 voices), 5 community searches for hindi, 1 rejected language, 1 rejected PII category
nodes.method: GET /list-voices and POST /search-community-voice with our key; validator error texts from create-agent probes; SDK type enums, 2026-10-20

nodes.title: Inference: Retell Platform Voices are mostly re-listed third-party voices. Of the 21 platform (retell-*) voices, 15 preview files are named minimax-*, 2 fish_audio-*, 1 cartesia-*, and 3 carry no provider tag; Cartesia previews sit in a folder named cartesia-sonic-3.6-2026-09-08. It rests on file names only (no audio or traffic), so treat the "self-hosted models" vendor claim as unproven rather than refuted.

Retell CRM contact create on India numbers: "9000000001" (10 digits) was stored as +19000000001; "09000000003" and "12345" were stored verbatim; "+919000000003" and "09000000003" coexisted as two contacts; only an identical string was refused as a duplicate. So a messy lead list yields wrong-country numbers and double contacts with no warning.
nodes.n: 6 contacts created, 1 duplicate attempt, all deleted afterwards
nodes.method: POST /create-contact with synthetic numbers on our org, read back the stored phone_number, 2026-10-20

nodes.title: Retell AI disclosure default depends on the creation path: the dashboard-seeded agent has handbook_config {ai_disclosure:true, default_personality:true}; an agent created through the API with only response_engine and voice_id has no handbook_config at all, although the docs say new agents get AI Disclosure When Asked by default. Whether the runtime still applies the preset was not tested on a call.
nodes.n: 2 agents compared (1 dashboard-seeded, 1 API-created, since deleted)
nodes.method: GET /get-agent on both after a bare POST /create-agent, 2026-10-20

nodes.title: Retell versioning: publishing freezes a version in place, and PATCH on a published version is refused (422 "Cannot update published agent other than version title"); create-agent-version(base_version) returns a draft and clones the response engine with it (agent v1 with llm v1); draft edits never publish. Agents carry prod and staging tags and calls freeze the tag used.

Retell lets a running call be steered by API: update-live-call appends additional_context to the transcript with role injected and can interrupt and regenerate (trigger_response); listen-live-call mints a subscribe-only token; take-over permanently stops the agent. This is a real mid-call control plane that a supervisor, a CRM event or a second model can drive.
Loading a CSV of contacts into Retell with an API key (upload-contact-import-file then create-contact-import with column mapping and default_country).
nodes.tried: POST /upload-contact-import-file with a synthetic 11-row messy CSV, GET /get-contact-import, and create-contact-import with a placeholder id, all with our Bearer key.
nodes.broke: Upload and status answer 401 "Unauthorized: Invalid JWT" although both are in the public OpenAPI and SDKs; create-contact-import validates but needs an upload id only the upload route can mint. The messy-CSV time-and-motion test therefore needs the dashboard login (or batch-call tasks, which are billable).

nodes.title: Proposed: from Retell's API, VP v1 should match these and beat them on the India path: (1) draft/publish with an engine cloned per version and frozen tags on calls; (2) per-call overrides (agent, variables, metadata) with an idempotency key; (3) a pre-answer inbound hook that can reject or reroute; (4) a live control plane for context injection and takeover; (5) typed per-product per-second cost on every call; (6) simulation tests with mocked tools. Beat: one contact object that normalises to E.164 with India as the default country and de-duplicates across formats; disclosure default-on on every creation path including the API; DNC/consent/window checks default-on for outbound; Indic-script pronunciation and Hindi-first voice catalogue; business-outcome codes beside the engineering disconnection reason; scriptable bulk import, export, batch status/cancel and aggregate analytics in the API, not only the dashboard.
nodes.rationale: Each match item exists in Retell's typed API and is something an Indian enterprise team building a renewal flow will expect; each beat item is a place where the same API shows a gap that the Indian complaint set (support, billing, account/UI, reliability) points at: wrong-country numbers, no dedupe, API-only agents without the disclosure preset, no batch status, JWT-only import and export.
nodes.reverse_if: The call battery shows Retell's defaults handle Hinglish turn-taking and disclosure better than assumed (the gap list then shrinks to import/export/analytics), or Indian buyers in the interview set rank any beat item below price and uptime.

nodes.title: Proposed: because setup is LLM-native (directive.2026-10-20.llm-native), VP exposes every dashboard action as an API/MCP operation with the same auth as the dashboard, so the chat builder and a customer's own agent can do everything a human can; Retell's JWT-only import/export and missing batch status/cancel are the counterexample.
nodes.rationale: Retell's own MCP server is two tools (search docs, run SDK code), so an agent can do only what the SDK can; the missing operations (import, export create, billing, analytics, batch list/cancel) are exactly what a chat-driven operator would be asked to do.
nodes.reverse_if: A chat builder shows no unmet need for these operations in the first 20 customer setup sessions.

nodes.title: What do Retell's real call_cost product lines, billed-duration scaling (prompt over 4,000 tokens), burst surcharge and default turn-taking look like on a Hinglish call, and does a bare API-created agent still say it is an AI when asked?
nodes.closes_when: The call-battery phase places calls on (a) a dashboard-built and (b) an API-built agent with the same prompt, reads call_cost.product_costs, llm_token_usage, latency and disconnection_reason, and asks "aap AI ho?" in at least 8 calls each.

nodes.title: How does a Retell batch call treat duplicates, Indian numbers without +91, empty variables, the do_not_call flag and calling windows when the CSV or tasks are realistic?
nodes.closes_when: A 50-row synthetic batch (to our own verified numbers only) is created in the call-battery phase and per-call results are read back with list-calls filtered by batch_call_id; the same rows are also tried through the dashboard CSV path.

nodes.title: Our Retell org still holds one synthetic agent (VP-SYNTHETIC-teardown-renewal-hinglish, v0 published, v1 draft) and its LLM engine with a fictional insurer prompt and an example.invalid webhook, next to the dashboard-seeded default agent. A later phase could mistake them for production or place a call on them.
nodes.mitigation: Name prefix VP-SYNTHETIC; reuse them in the call-battery phase or delete them first; the contacts, flow and test definition were already deleted; never attach a real number or webhook to them.

nodes.title: Sarvam authorized-surface phase: 55 graded claims (39 observed, 7 inferred, 7 vendor-claimed, 2 unknown) from 29 authorized requests with our own Model API keys (plus 6 unauthenticated GETs of public MCP OAuth metadata), the live Voice Agents and Model API OpenAPI files, 52 re-fetched docs pages, four published SDK packages (Python and npm, conv-ai and model SDKs) and one REA run on the npm conv-ai SDK. No call, number, agent or other billable action; the Voice Agents control plane refused both keys, so no Voice Agents object was read or created.
Using the stored Sarvam keys (Model API class) against the Voice Agents control plane to create and read back an agent, list deployments or read analytics.
nodes.tried: One read-only GET per route on apps.sarvam.ai (analytics query-schema, app-authoring deployments, app-runtime signed-URL) with all-zero UUID scope, with X-API-Key, Bearer and the Model API header, using both the SARVAM2 and the SARVAM team key. The same keys returned 200 on api.sarvam.ai/v2/models.
nodes.broke: Every Voice Agents route answered 401 "Invalid API key format" (X-API-Key) or "Malformed token" / "Invalid Bearer token" (Bearer). Voice Agents needs a separate workspace key made in the dashboard (Settings > API Key); the Model API key is a different class. So no agent config JSON, deployment, campaign, cohort or call log could be read, and the lane relied on the OpenAPI, SDKs and docs for the Voice Agents data model.

nodes.title: Sarvam publishes a 68-operation Voice Agents REST API (analytics 24, scheduling 19, evals 15, app-authoring 6, outbounds 1, BYOK 3) and a 53-operation Model API; the Voice Agents spec has no agent create/edit/commit, telephony, knowledge-base, voice, secrets, API-key or DND operations (the docs name a DND API the spec lacks), so agent authoring lives only in the dashboard, Genie and the MCP server.
nodes.n: 68 Voice Agents operations, 175 schemas; 53 Model API operations
nodes.method: script over the live OpenAPI files (docs.sarvam.ai/openapi/voice-agents.json and apis.json, fetched 2026-10-20, voice-agents spec identical to the public-phase copy) grouped by service base URL; absence checked by path and keyword search (0 matches for dnd, dlt, ncpr)

nodes.title: Sarvam webhooks are post-call only (campaign attempt, inbound call, instant outbound), with {url, metadata} as the whole config: no signature or secret field, no mid-call hook, English-only transcripts (en_text), delivery records running/completed/failed and re-delivery of up to 200 attempts. Mid-call integration is the opposite direction: the agent calls the customer HTTPS tool, on-start/on-end hooks or Python code tools.

Sarvam artefacts disagree with each other: three language lists (OpenAPI 13 with Sanskrit, Python SDK 13 with Konkani, npm SDK 11), different audio rates (Python in 16/48 kHz, npm in 8/16 kHz), the npm SDK is 7 months behind Python (0.0.42 vs 1.1.1), 12 documented doc-vs-spec mismatches in all (e.g. a DND API and ConnectionConfig fields that the spec lacks).
nodes.n: 3 SDK/spec artefacts compared; 12 mismatches recorded
nodes.method: scripted diff of enums in the OpenAPI, sarvam-conv-ai-sdk 1.1.1 (PyPI wheel) and 0.0.42 (npm tarball), plus manual reading of 52 docs pages, 2026-10-20

nodes.title: Turn-taking lives in Sarvam's STT service: the realtime STT WebSocket exposes ten frame-level VAD parameters (thresholds, min speech frames, negative-frame window, interrupt frames, pre-speech pad, volume gate) while the agent builder offers only three coarse settings (interrupt on/off, sound sensitivity, eagerness) plus nudges. Mapping builder sliders to those parameters is inferred, not documented.

Sarvam sells voices as job-tagged personas: 222 v4-flash slugs named name_language_style across 50 style tokens (customer 15, recovery 10, companion 11, sales 5, banking 5, insurance 3; hi 116, en 62, enhi 13); the docs say 176 voices while the API enum has 266 slugs.

Proposed: add to the v1 parity floor what Sarvam's API already gives buyers: attempt and interaction records with failure reason and ended-by, cohort validation with a downloadable rejected-records file, retry ladder by outcome class, per-user number rotation, first-class transfer records, stereo recordings, post-call webhooks with re-delivery, an eval API with a judge, a SQL analytics API and typed SDKs plus an MCP server.
nodes.rationale: Each exists in Sarvam's live spec at INR 3-3.5/min (claims SAC-14 to SAC-23, SAC-29, SAC-33, SAC-34), so an Indian enterprise buyer comparing against it will expect them. They are a floor, not a wedge, in line with the 2026-10-17 rejection of parity-undercut.
nodes.reverse_if: Buyer interviews show Indian operations leads never use failure-reason filters, rejected-record downloads, evals or SQL boards (a no-code-only buyer), or usability sessions show a simpler model wins the same tasks.

nodes.title: Proposed: aim VP's differentiation at the places Sarvam's API is thin: user-visible model and voice choice, signed webhooks, mid-call function hooks, a usage and cost API, cross-call memory, consent/DND/window objects with category-aware calling hours, and an agent-authoring REST API that is as complete as the dashboard.
nodes.rationale: Sarvam's spec has no model picker or BYO (temperature only), WebhookConfig is url plus metadata with no signing, no mid-call callback, no usage/balance endpoint, memory is per call with caller context pulled from the customer, and compliance is "your responsibility" with free-form calling windows. These are measurable gaps on tasks we can run in the call-battery phase.
nodes.reverse_if: Interviews show buyers do not value these (they take a closed bundle at INR 3-3.5 without wanting hooks or signing), or Sarvam ships them (watch changelog/OpenAPI hash).

nodes.title: Needed: a Voice Agents workspace API key (dashboard Settings > API Key) or a dashboard session on the SARVAM2 account. Without it we still lack: an agent's full config JSON, version history, telephony connection and number objects, KB ingestion, query-schema table list, a messy-CSV cohort validation, schedule-window enforcement, voicemail/transfer behaviour, call logs and ledger lines.
nodes.closes_when: The owner or Instinct creates a workspace key (kept in the scratchpad env file) or lets a dashboard phase run; then create and read back one synthetic agent, a paused future campaign with a 50-row messy cohort, a test suite run (INR 2) and the query-schema list, and score pre-registered predictions SAR-P01 to P08.

nodes.title: Inference (weighted by the 0.85 Bolna blind-calibration hit rate): patterns in Bolna's code that closed vendors' APIs also expose: history trimmed to what the caller heard (ElevenLabs agent_response_correction), speculative generation at early end of turn (ElevenLabs speculative_turn, metered separately), a cheap separate model for post-call judges, LLM-classified voicemail on transcript text, and component-partial failover (LLM at Bolna, TTS at Retell, STT/LLM at Vapi, scheduled model reroute at ElevenLabs; no carrier failover anywhere).

Proposed VP v1 object model: Org/Workspace (wallet, spend cap, concurrency on the API); Agent with draft/publish versions and a materialised resolved config; Deployment pinning a version or split; Contact as a first-class object (India-default E.164, cross-format dedupe, consent ledger, DND/NCPR, attempt history, memory slot for v2); Campaign as a policy (call category -> window, retry ladder by outcome, attempt budget, pacing, caller-ID pool, built-in predial check); Attempt separate from Conversation; customer-owned Outcome/Judge definitions; signed webhooks; INR cost lines. Consolidates the lane proposals acct-vapi-contact-compliance-layer, acct-vapi-one-publish-model and acct-sarvam-parity-floor-items.
nodes.rationale: The convergent shape across five APIs is agent + call + post-call judge; every gap they share sits on the person and the policy (contact, consent, windows, retries, outcomes), which is where Indian enterprise calling is regulated and where 70% of Indian complaints sit (support, billing, account/UI).
nodes.reverse_if: Usability sessions or the first buyer interviews show a contact-centric model slows first-campaign setup with no drop in errors, or the walk-through finds an incumbent dashboard already ships contacts with consent, windows and retries that its API hides.

nodes.title: Proposed v1 API parity floor, confirmed from at least 4 of 5 incumbent APIs (not marketing): versioned agents with pinning; per-call overrides and variables; a pre-call decision hook; HTTP tools, transfer and end-call; post-call webhook with the full record; typed per-call cost; post-call LLM judge with typed extraction; simulated-caller tests; campaign create/status/cancel; knowledge bases; SIP/number import; an MCP server. Parity, not wedge.
nodes.rationale: An Indian enterprise evaluating VP against these platforms will expect each item; each is shipped by 4-5 of 5 vendors per api-surface-matrix.csv.
nodes.reverse_if: Buyer interviews (10-15 operations leads) rank an item as unused (Kano indifferent), or the dashboard walk-through finds a must-have the APIs did not show.

nodes.title: Proposed 5 places to beat, each gapped in every incumbent API and tied to a runnable task: (1) contact-and-compliance layer on by default (task: messy 50-row CSV + window battery); (2) Hinglish turn-taking that never discards a short reply and listens during the opening (task: 'nahi/haan/ruko/bas' over the agent, 2.4 s pause); (3) the stored config is what runs: materialised defaults, unknown fields refused, voice-language checks, model-in-effect per call, disclosure on every creation path (task: create by API, read back, call, compare); (4) owned outcomes and economics: business outcome beside the engineering code, visible editable judges, cost and funnel by campaign/contact, per-second billing (task: find a failed call and why; cost one campaign); (5) dashboard parity on the API and MCP for chat-driven setup (task: chat builder runs a campaign end to end with no dashboard).
nodes.rationale: Parity plus undercut was rejected (rejected.2026-10-17.parity-undercut) and incumbents have the margin to follow on price (XS-30); these five are gaps visible in their own typed APIs and match the Indian complaint classes, and each can be scored as task success.
nodes.reverse_if: The walk-through or call battery shows incumbents pass these tasks, or buyer interviews do not rank the failures as switching reasons; for (2), VP's own stack fails to beat them on the same battery.

Claiming it before measuring both sides on one battery would repeat a parity-style claim without evidence.

nodes.title: Vapi: every assistant PATCH publishes an immutable version (v1 then v2, parentVersion, configHash); drafts are separate sparse records with a baseVersion and two coexisted for one assistant; a name-only assistant stores no model, voice or turn-taking fields, so the stored record does not show what will run. Traffic splits are an append-only ledger (actor type and key id recorded) that outlives the assistant.

Vapi's Call.endedReason has 638 values: 300 call.in-progress.error-*, 270 pipeline-error-*, 20 call.start.error-*, 5 ringing, 2 forwarding, 2 other call.*, 39 plain (customer-busy, voicemail, silence-timed-out...). All are engineering codes keyed to a provider; none expresses a business outcome (agreed, call back, refused, wrong number, DND).

Indian complaints concentrate on usability, support and billing, and these objects are where an operator's daily work happens. The same layer serves pre-sale and post-sale calling.

nodes.title: Proposed: VP uses one publish path (draft, test, publish, ramp) where an ordinary edit never publishes, stored assistants are shown with a resolved-config view (the effective STT, LLM, TTS, endpointing and interruption lists), and splits cannot silently pin out a later fix.

That combination matches complaints that a draft does not hold the prompt. The cost of our version is a clearer state machine and one extra screen.

nodes.title: Inference: Bolna default-stack COGS about INR 2.0-3.8 per connected min (mid ~2.8) at FX 95; all-in buyer price INR 4.2-8.0/min depending on tier and whether the $0.02 platform fee sits on top; voice-bundle gross margin 46-72% at PAYG, 18-58% at the AWS annual ~4 cents rate. A reported INR 1.75-2 enterprise rate is at or below default-stack COGS, which is consistent with the Mumbai self-hosted inference build-out seen in certificate transparency.

Bolna India plumbing is reactive. No NCPR/DND scrub. Consent is only 'upload proof of opt-in' after a telephony-provider violation report. Calling guardrails are off by default, whole-hour only, with a bypass flag. DLT/PE registration and the RBI/SEBI certificate for the 160-series are left to the buyer. Number KYC needs a CIN and accepts only Pvt Ltd companies. India residency is Enterprise-only and requires Plivo + Azure OpenAI with no BYOK.

Bolna already ships LLM-native setup, so VP's chat-driven setup is parity, not a wedge, against Bolna. It has Studio Auto Build (brief to agent), Ask Bolna in the dashboard, edit-prompt-by-chat (2026-09-09), an MCP server listed as a Claude connector (2026-10-09) and 20 Skills for coding assistants. What is missing: no contact/CRM object, no cross-call memory, no customer-facing optimisation loop.

Does Bolna charge the $0.02/min platform fee on top of the bundled 6-cent rate, or only under BYOK? What does telephony cost per minute on Bolna-hosted Indian numbers? These two unknowns move Bolna's all-in price between INR ~6.1 and ~8.0/min at PAYG.

nodes.title:
Bolna turn-taking in code (cascade path):
- Barge-in only fires when an interim transcript has MORE than N words (dashboard N=2, so 3 words) or exactly equals an English stop phrase. Provider speech-start never interrupts.
- A final of N words or fewer spoken over the agent is discarded, so short Hindi replies ('haan ji', 'nahi', 'ruko') are lost.
- A speculative LLM request starts on Deepgram Flux EagerEndOfTurn.
- From turn 3 on, the agent's audio is held for incremental_delay ms.
- In S2S mode the provider's VAD barges in.
This is a testable where-we-win item.

Inference: Bolna serves its own models. Provider 'bolna' ASR defaults to nemotron-asr-hi over the OpenAI Realtime transcription protocol, a 'bolna' LLM provider is treated as self-hosted, and DEEPGRAM_HOST is overridable. So their per-minute COGS on own-model calls sits below the INR 2.0-3.8 default-stack reconstruction (BOL-37), and they have more room to cut price.

v2 note: at bc59921 Bolna's engine still has no cross-call memory and no A/B, bandit or prompt-optimisation loop (confirms l4a at 8e300d9). It already emits the per-call signals such a loop would consume: interruption counts, barge-in recovery, talk-listen time, longest monologue, user-bot latency, and dead air inside replies.

Bolna's engine has 0 lines of India calling-compliance logic (no DND, DLT, NCPR, consent or calling-window code), so anything that exists lives in the closed scheduler or with the buyer. Deepgram's model-improvement opt-out is per agent and, when unset, the env defaults to not opted out; the hosted value is unknown.
