nodes.title: Where the dashboard differs from the earlier Retell research: (1) RET-09 said RBAC is Enterprise-only, but the free trial shows three fixed System roles (Admin, Developer, Member) with custom Add Role greyed out and no SSO page; (2) the earlier default timezone was America/Los_Angeles, but the batch Schedule form defaults to Asia/Calcutta; (3) the model picker lists 33 cascaded models where the API enum count was 32; (4) the Call History table has a Session Outcome column, which may partly cover the business-outcome gap; (5) there is no Campaigns screen in the navigation, so the server-side Campaigns object has no visible dashboard surface; (6) the dashboard DNC copy conflicts with the docs on batch DNC. Confirmed: contact memory read ON and update OFF, burst enabled, Persona gate at number purchase, first 10 KBs free, US-centric PII categories, no Indian IDs.

Proposed parity floor for VP v1 from Retell's dashboard (match, not beat): a per-row price in the model picker plus a Cost / Latency / Tokens strip for the current selection; Test Audio and Test LLM panel with a version and environment marker; a Simulation tab of test cases with success criteria; a lifecycle Workflow view with pre-call and post-call function slots; post-call extraction defaulting to summary, success and sentiment; three-mode transfer (cold, warm, agentic warm) explained in plain language; KB sources of web pages, files, text, Google Drive, OneDrive and Notion; per-feature prices shown at the toggle; ops pages for live monitoring, alerts, dashboards with breakdown, AI QA and call history with cost and latency columns; limits, API keys with a webhook-signing badge, and fixed roles.
nodes.rationale: These are the surfaces an Indian enterprise team will expect from any Retell-class product and none of them is a differentiator in itself; owner intent is parity made better (directive.2026-10-20.intent-better-product).
nodes.reverse_if: Buyer interviews or the call battery show these are not switching factors, or open.2026-10-20.parity-floor-vs-wedge resolves to a narrower floor.

nodes.title: Proposed places for VP to beat Retell's dashboard, each with a task: (1) an India-aware batch form with consent and DND/NCPR scrub, default 09:00-21:00 IST windows with a legal-hours warning, retries, per-lead windows, an agent selector and a stated reason when Send is disabled; (2) Indic discoverability: language filter and Indian-accent and Hinglish tags on voices, Hindi vocabulary sets, a visible language-hold control; (3) PII categories with Aadhaar and PAN and privacy-first defaults; (4) conservative defaults for silence hang-up and max duration with a spend cap, and burst or surcharge options off until chosen; (5) a cost strip that itemises ASR, LLM, voice, telephony and platform; (6) empty states with a call to action, Sample labels on demo data, tours scoped to their page; (7) turn-taking controls in milliseconds with Hindi-aware labels (a hypothesis until a battery measures it); (8) a number path that states KYC time and cost before the user commits.
nodes.rationale: Each item is a gap visible in the Retell dashboard captures and matches Indian complaint classes from earlier research; none is proven to be a switching reason.
nodes.reverse_if: A call battery shows Retell defaults handle Hinglish turn-taking and compliance as well as VP, or the owner narrows v1 scope.

nodes.title: Defaults a new Sarvam agent carries, read from the dashboard: voice Shubh; per-language voices OFF; speed 1.15x; pitch 0.00; volume 1.0; background sound 'Quiet office' (volume about one third); switch language during call ON with 11 languages preselected and Hindi as the locked starting language; Output numbers in Indic ON (partly hidden); idle nudge 'Hey, are you still on the call?' after 5 s; hang up after unanswered nudges ON; voicemail ON with a default message that names no company or purpose; call forwarding OFF; max call length 15 min (up to 60); model temperature 'Balanced' (no number); greeting 'Hi, I am Shubh calling from Sarvam...'. Not captured: the Listening defaults and the knowledge-base row.

Inference from the Sarvam dashboard: no millisecond value for endpointing, hold or interruption appears anywhere in the captured builder (only a 5 s nudge delay and a 15 min call cap), and the Listening section (barge-in, eagerness, volume threshold) has no screenshot, only the evaluator's note. Together with the account-phase finding of three coarse controls over ten VAD parameters, a builder cannot see, sum or tune a reply floor, unlike Bolna's visible 500 ms + 900 ms sliders. Whether Sarvam's defaults are Hindi-tuned or English-tuned is unknown without a live call.

Inference from the Sarvam dashboard: the LLM and ASR are not user choices (only a temperature slider and a TTS voice picker appear), the voice minute is one bundled Rs 3-3.5 rate, and no latency, cost or quality figure is shown per voice or per model at the point of choice; the only latency number is an aggregate analytics KPI and an unquantified '40% faster' V4 claim. Vapi and ElevenLabs show per-option latency and cost inline. A visible, curated, per-option trade-off display is open ground for VP.

Observed in the Sarvam dashboard: a new agent defaults to 'Quiet office' background sound ON, and the voice catalogue sells 'AI Companion', 'Warm Night Companion' and 'Therapist Voice' personas; no AI-disclosure setting appears on any captured settings screen (bounded negative; the Listening and knowledge-base rows were not captured). Sarvam's own template prompt preview does contain an instruction to say 'a virtual assistant' when asked whether the caller is speaking to an AI, so disclosure sits in the prompt, not in an enforced control, which agrees with the 6 of 6 'claimed human' result on the EMI demo.

Observed in the Sarvam campaign wizard (4 steps: Agent, Recipients, Schedule, Review & Launch): step 1 asks for campaign name, agent, version and a telephony connection with numbers (By number / By group), and raises an inline 'This version is not committed' gate with a one-click 'Commit version' button. No consent, DND, DLT, calling-window or retry field appears on step 1 or on the empty state; DND appears only as an API recipe card. Steps 2-4 and the Indian number KYC were not captured, so absence beyond step 1 is unknown.

Proposed from the Sarvam dashboard: treat as the parity floor a prompt-box agent creator with India-vertical templates, a docked Voice/Phone/Chat test panel, input and output variables with extraction prompts and a call goal, API tools with cURL import and inline Send, Mock API and validator/verifier tools, per-language voices and a pronunciation dictionary, nudge and hang-up and voicemail settings, a 4-step campaign wizard with an inline commit gate, call logs with failure reasons, a one-click MCP install page and API recipe cards, and an INR plan table with per-pulse rates. Beat it by (1) showing predicted reply gap, latency and cost beside every turn-taking, model and voice choice, (2) putting consent, DND and category-aware calling windows inside the campaign steps, (3) a persistent preflight checklist instead of discovering gates at deploy time, (4) a non-removable AI disclosure with no default fake ambience, (5) explicit empty, loading and error states and a visible overdrawn state, (6) a voice catalogue honest about depth per language.
nodes.rationale: Each parity item is observed on a trial account and is table stakes for an Indian buyer coming from Sarvam; each beat item answers a specific gap in the captures (hidden numbers, blank pages, late gates, unlabelled negative balance). Parity is a floor, not a wedge (rejected.2026-10-17.parity-undercut), so v1 has to win on measured task failures.
nodes.reverse_if: A live battery shows Sarvam's coarse turn-taking and bundled models match or beat VP's visible controls on reply gap and cut-in rate, so that exposing numbers adds no measured benefit; or the unseen Sarvam steps (campaign steps 2-4, Listening, Policy) turn out to contain the consent, DND and window controls listed as missing.

nodes.title: Cross-vendor dashboard walkthrough synthesis (Vapi, Retell, Bolna, ElevenLabs, Sarvam, Exotel; captured 2026-10-21 by Instinct, no live call, no number bought). Observed in the captures: 0 of 6 campaign or batch forms carry a consent, DND/NCPR or DLT field; 0 of 6 builders show a predicted reply gap; the displayed latency and cost headlines (Vapi, Retell, Bolna) are component sums that leave out telephony and the end-of-turn wait; 0 of 6 walkthroughs reached a ring on an Indian line; 0 of 6 offer a Hinglish or code-mixed language option; 5 of 6 ship an in-dashboard chat assistant (none exercised). The synthesis re-opened 84 screenshots and corrected 9 vendor-analyst claims from the pixels.

nodes.n: 6 vendor dashboards; 84 screenshots re-opened by the synthesis plus the vendor analysts' reading of the text captures and Instinct's notes (each cell graded)
nodes.method: Default values read from the dashboard captures of 2026-10-21 as left by the vendor on a trial account, not configured by us and not exercised on a call. Cells are graded observed-in-pixels, observed-in-text-capture, notes-only, API read-back of 2026-10-20, or unknown.
nodes.title: Cross-vendor conversation and campaign defaults as captured. End-of-turn: Vapi 1.5 s fixed wait (0-3 s), Intelligent Turn-Taking off; Retell 0 ms added wait, interruption sensitivity 0.9; Bolna endpointing 500 ms + linear delay 900 ms, 1 word to interrupt (saved agent of unknown origin); ElevenLabs eagerness Normal, Turn V3, 7 s take-turn (API read-back); Sarvam and Exotel show no turn-taking numbers. Silence hang-up: Retell 10 min, Bolna 20 s, ElevenLabs disabled, Sarvam after unanswered 5 s nudges, Exotel after 3 nudges at 7 s. Max call: Retell 1 h, Bolna 90 s, ElevenLabs 600 s, Sarvam 15 min, Exotel off. Calling window: Retell 00:00-23:59 Mon-Sun, Bolna 09:00-21:00 per agent, ElevenLabs start time plus Asia/Calcutta only. Burst on by default at Retell (+USD 0.10/min) and ElevenLabs (API read-back).

Observed in the dashboards: none of the six campaign or batch creation surfaces (vapi 83-campaign-create, retell 24/25, bolna 22-new-campaign-dialog, elevenlabs 33/35, sarvam-25/26 step 1, exotel-10) has a consent source, DND/NCPR scrub or DLT field. Default windows are 00:00-23:59 Mon-Sun (Retell) or 09:00-21:00 set per agent in whole hours (Bolna); ElevenLabs has a start time and a timezone only. The only call-category field seen anywhere is Exotel's Transactional vs Promotional call type (Instinct's notes, not in pixels), and it is not shown driving a window. Retell's DNC toggle (13-security-shot) is in-call opt-out capture, off by default; Sarvam's DND list appears only as an API recipe card. Vapi steps 2-3 and Sarvam steps 2-4 were not reached.

Observed: no dashboard shows a predicted reply gap or sums its turn-taking settings, and the units differ by vendor: seconds slider (Vapi End-of-Turn Wait 1.5 s, vapi 80-transcriber-languages), milliseconds with no sum (Bolna 500 + 900 ms, bolna 16-builder-Engine), an enum plus seconds (ElevenLabs eagerness Normal, elevenlabs 44-agent-settings), an added-wait slider whose handle sits at the far right beside 0 ms (Retell, retell 09-model-dropdown), or nothing visible (Sarvam Listening not captured; Exotel VAD empty). No dashboard ships an editable Hindi or Hinglish backchannel or interruption list; Vapi's smart endpointing is labelled English-only and ElevenLabs Turn V3 locks ASR to Scribe v2 Realtime. Whether any of these defaults suit Hinglish is unmeasured.

Inference from displayed numbers: per-minute and latency headlines are component sums. Vapi ~1,530 ms = 410 + 690 + 430 and ~USD 0.09 = 0.05 hosting + components, excluding the 1.5 s wait and telephony (vapi 33-riley-assistant); our measured Vapi demo-agent clean-turn p50 was 2,319 ms (2026-10-17, different agent). Retell USD 0.134 = 0.055 + 0.015 + 0.064, excluding telephony (retell 09). Bolna USD 0.060 = 3.5 + 0.5 + 2 cents with a 30 s pulse on all three lines, displayed as about INR 5.72 (bolna 34-account, 40-recharge-dialog). ElevenLabs shows a latency range and USD/min per LLM row, but ranges span up to about 10x (for example 844 ms to 8.93 s) and the per-minute price is 1.7-2.3x below its own API calculator at the same message rate (elevenlabs 61-llm-list). Bolna, Sarvam and Exotel show no per-option latency or price.

Observed defaults that hold lines open or raise spend without a choice by the buyer: Retell burst ON (up to 3x concurrency at +USD 0.10/min, retell 5x-settings), silence hang-up 10 min and max call 1 h (text capture), data kept 'Everything, Keep forever' (retell 13-security-shot); ElevenLabs all 9 system tools OFF including End conversation and Voicemail detection (elevenlabs 42-agent-tools), silence end-call Disabled, bursting on (API read-back), retention Unlimited; Exotel max call duration off (notes); Vapi recording consent gated to Enterprise (vapi 34-builder-Advanced). No spend cap was seen in any dashboard (Retell's Budget Setting was not opened). At Retell's displayed USD 0.134/min a 10-minute silent line is about USD 1.34 and a 1-hour call about USD 8.04 (inferred).

Observed: no walkthrough reached a ring on an Indian line, and each stopped at a different gate. Vapi free numbers are US area codes and inbound-only (vapi 06c-free-vapi-number); Retell asks for Persona identity verification before showing any country or price (retell 30-buy-number-shot); ElevenLabs numbers are import-only, and its Exotel import needs 7 fields with Region defaulting to Singapore under +91 (elevenlabs 34-phone-exotel-form); Bolna shows India with Plivo or Vobiz but 'No compliance applications found. Create one' before Subscribe, and its Vobiz KYC accepts PAN + Aadhaar for persons (bolna 25, 36-account-Vobiz-KYC); Sarvam offers Rent (Powered by Vobiz) or bring-your-own with 7 providers, flows not opened (sarvam-23); Exotel needs KYC and payment with GST details (exotel-01, notes). W7 (minutes to first Indian ring) is untested on both sides.

Pixel checks of vendor-analyst claims (2026-10-21): (1) Retell's DNC toggle copy in pixels is in-call opt-out capture, not 'skip DNC contacts' (retell 13); (2) ElevenLabs batch does state why Submit is off, in the phone field placeholder, but gives no link to fix it (elevenlabs 33); (3) Exotel Campaigns has a CREATE NEW button above the empty table (exotel-09); (4) Exotel agent pages carry an unexercised 'Talk to Agent' primary button, so 'phone-only testing' is unproven (exotel-02); (5) Exotel Rollout describes a traffic split but shows no split control (exotel-04-rollout); (6) Bolna's India compliance row names the fix with a 'Create one' link (bolna 25); (7) Retell's analytics tiles show 0, 0s and 0ms on empty data, the same zero/no-data conflation flagged at Sarvam (retell 43, sarvam-29); (8) Retell's persistent checklist and stale tour overlay the flow-builder palette and canvases (retell 76, 80); (9) ElevenLabs LLM latency ranges reach about 10x (elevenlabs 61).

Proposed changes to the 21-item v1 must-be list after the dashboard walkthroughs. Add: (A) price and India-measured latency at every stack choice plus an all-in per-minute headline that includes telephony, pulse and turn wait; (B) contacts with India-default E.164, DND status and attempt history (memory slot reserved for v2); (C) bounded call and spend defaults: end-call on, silence hang-up on, max duration set, burst opt-in, spend cap; (D) state integrity: no click creates or publishes, an unsaved indicator, and a stated reason plus fix beside every disabled primary action. Promote AI disclosure from a VP rule to a must-be on every creation path, templates included. Sharpen: browser and text test with no number; CSV contract shown before upload with per-row overrides; retries and windows on the campaign form, window defaulted from call category; DNC honoured on batch, campaign, API and single call, with in-call opt-out on by default; a Hinglish mode and language-filtered voices; INR rate table with pulse units; fixed roles on every plan. Move India data residency from a self-serve UI must-be to an architecture and contract item (no dashboard exposes it).
nodes.rationale: Each change is tied to a capture: 6 of 6 campaign forms lack compliance fields; 3 of 6 pickers show price or latency and 3 show none; Retell, ElevenLabs and Exotel defaults leave lines open or spend unbounded; Vapi click-to-publish, Bolna and Sarvam missing unsaved state and silent disabled buttons at Vapi and Retell; 0 of 6 offer Hinglish; 0 of 6 expose residency. Parity items stay parity (open.2026-10-20.parity-floor-vs-wedge); the wedge is still measured task failure.
nodes.reverse_if: Buyer interviews rank any added item outside the top half of switching reasons, or 5-user usability sessions show buyers complete the same tasks on an incumbent dashboard without the added item at equal time and error rates, or two or more incumbents ship the item by default before VP v1.

nodes.title: Proposed: VP's turn-taking panel shows every timing in milliseconds with its range, sums them into a predicted reply gap next to the measured India p50 for that preset, ships Hindi and Hinglish backchannel, stop and acknowledgement lists as editable defaults (never discarding short replies), exposes listen-during-opening, and offers three named presets. Defaults come from VP's own battery, not from this document.
nodes.rationale: No incumbent dashboard shows a predicted gap or a Hindi lexicon; units differ across Vapi (s), Bolna (ms), ElevenLabs (enum) and Retell (added-wait slider), and Sarvam and Exotel hide the controls. VP's own stacks still cut in on 15-42% of turns, so the panel is a design commitment, not a claimed advantage.
nodes.reverse_if: The stereo Hinglish call battery shows an incumbent's defaults at or below VP on p50 reply gap and cut-in rate, or usability sessions show buyers do not open or understand the panel and presets alone carry the outcome.

nodes.title: Proposed: every model, voice and transcriber row in VP shows India-measured p50 and p90 latency (with n and date), INR per minute, supported Indian languages and a sample, and the agent header shows an all-in INR per connected minute that includes telephony, pulse rounding and the turn wait. Vendor-displayed figures, if shown, are labelled as vendor numbers.
nodes.rationale: Vapi and ElevenLabs show per-row metrics but their headlines omit telephony and the wait, ElevenLabs ranges span about 10x and its price assumption is unstated, Retell shows price only, and Bolna, Sarvam and Exotel show nothing per option. The stack is a user choice in VP (decision.2026-10-20.product-stack-selectable), so the trade-off display carries the choice.
nodes.reverse_if: Usability sessions show buyers pick from presets and never open per-row data, or measured India latency per option varies so little across the catalogue that one number per preset suffices.

nodes.title: Proposed: VP's campaign form takes the call category first (service, transactional, promotional), derives the allowed window and number series from it, and carries consent source, DND/NCPR scrub status, retries by outcome, an attempt cap and a per-contact local-time window as fields with defaults on; the CSV contract and a row-level preview with reasons show before launch; any disabled Launch names the blocking item and links to its fix.
nodes.rationale: No incumbent campaign form has these fields (6 of 6 observed); windows default to 00:00-23:59 (Retell) or a whole-hour agent setting (Bolna); Bolna needs a published workflow before a campaign; Vapi and Retell disable the primary button with no reason, while Sarvam's inline commit gate and Bolna's 'Create one' link show the pattern that names the fix. Post-sale reminders (decision.2026-10-20.synthesis-postsale-first) depend on these.
nodes.reverse_if: Counsel holds that service calls need no window or scrub and buyers reject the extra fields in usability sessions, or an incumbent ships category-driven windows and scrub by default before VP v1 (W1 kill bar).

nodes.title: Proposed UI rules for VP: no menu or dropdown click creates, saves or publishes anything; drafts show an unsaved marker until saved; publish is explicit with a diff; every disabled primary action shows its reason and a link to the fix; empty, zero, loading and failed states are visually distinct (no fake chart lines, no '0 ms' on empty data); sample data is labelled as sample.
nodes.rationale: Observed hazards: Vapi published a tool on a menu click and autosaved a draft on a dropdown choice (vapi 57); Bolna shows no unsaved marker (bolna 21) and Sarvam has no save control (sarvam-03); Vapi and Retell disable Next or Send without a reason (vapi 83, retell 24); Exotel shows generic 'Unable to load' toasts (exotel-10); Sarvam draws a wavy line on no data (sarvam-29), Retell and Sarvam show 0 ms latency on empty data, Retell shows unlabelled sample QA data (retell 46). ElevenLabs' '---' plus 'No data has been collected' (elevenlabs 7-analytics) shows the correct pattern.
nodes.reverse_if: Usability sessions show no task errors attributable to these states on the incumbent dashboards, or the rules measurably slow expert users (for example explicit publish adds more than 10% to build time with no error reduction).

nodes.title: Ordered evidence plan after the walkthroughs: (1) a no-cost second dashboard pass with below-the-fold screenshots and a no-click-to-create rule (Bolna New Agent Engine and Calling tabs, Vapi Advanced slider values, Sarvam Listening, Retell call settings and Agent Handbook disclosure, ElevenLabs Agent behavior and voice language filter, Exotel create form and Talk to Agent, contradiction re-checks); (2) messy-CSV uploads to draft or paused campaigns with the fail-closed renderer; (3) screen-recorded T0 sign-up to first Indian ring per vendor with owner-approved KYC and numbers; (4) the stereo Hinglish call battery, Bolna first, on dashboard-created default agents including T9c disclosure; (5) the T7 billing audit at 30, 45 and 90 s; (6) 5-user human usability sessions on the same tasks.
nodes.closes_when: Each step has produced its artefact: pass-2 captures with the listed screens; per-vendor CSV outcome scores out of 50; T0 minutes per vendor; battery p50/p90 reply gap, cut-in rate and short-reply handling per vendor with n of 30 or more clean turns; invoice-versus-rate-card deltas; usability task times and error counts.

nodes.title: Walkthrough captures and procedure carry hazards: retell 08-call-transfer-form.png shows a full +1 transfer number in clear (origin unknown), Exotel captures 11 and 12 show the owner's phone in clear and 13 is partly redacted, one Bolna screen shows a vendor contact email, and Instinct's notes carry a person's name; clicking menus in Vapi created and published a tool and saved a draft on the vendor account.
nodes.mitigation: Keep data/walkthroughs out of commits and published pages (data/ is gitignored); quote numbers and emails only as [phone redacted] / [email redacted]; in the next pass, never click Create-type menus and capture option lists from text instead; list every vendor-side object created in the session log.

nodes.title: Inference from the Vapi dashboard: the headline '~1,530 ms' on the assistant page is exactly the sum of the three component latencies (Soniox 410 + GPT-4.1 690 + Vapi voice 430), so it leaves out the 1.5 s End-of-Turn Wait, telephony transport and the handset side. The '~$0.09/min' headline is about $0.05 hosting plus $0.004 + $0.02 + $0.02 components (= $0.094) and leaves out telephony; the cost bar's teal segment is about 53% of the bar, matching hosting. Both are vendor-displayed numbers, not measured.

Vapi dashboard catalogue sizes as displayed on 2026-10-21: about 92 LLM rows (about 14 repeated or deprecated), 45 voice-model rows, 40 transcriber rows, 57 transcriber languages plus Automatic, 15 Create Tool types, 52 Integrations tiles, 12 stock voices in the library grid (2 Indian-accented, both 'Indian American'). Every row shows latency, price per minute and one quality score as displayed by the vendor.
nodes.n: 7 lists counted from 7 text captures of one trial org (51-voice-model-dropdown, 52-model-dropdown, 53-transcriber-model-dropdown, 80-transcriber-languages, 56-create-tool-menu-items, 63-integrations, 75-voice-library)

nodes.title: Observed in the Vapi dashboard: the Soniox language picker lists 57 languages but only Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, Marathi, Urdu (and Nepali) from South Asia, with no Bengali, Telugu, Gujarati, Malayalam or Punjabi, although the API enum lists 12 Indic codes for Soniox. No Indian speech vendor appears in any picker or in the 52-tile Integrations catalogue. The voice library shows 12 voices, two Indian-accented and both labelled 'Indian American'. The dashboard picker is narrower than the API, so a dashboard-only buyer sees less Indic coverage than exists.

Observed Vapi dashboard turn-taking surface: Intelligent Turn-Taking is OFF by default with a fixed End-of-Turn Wait of 1.5 s (0-3 s); the Advanced tab exposes Wait Seconds (0-5), Smart Endpointing (Off or LiveKit, English only), punctuation waits (0-3 s each) and three stop-speaking sliders (words 0-10, voice seconds 0-0.5, back-off 0-10) but no editable acknowledgement or interruption phrase lists. The 1.5 s default is the same order as Bolna's inferred 1.4 s reply floor; whether it adds to the 0.4 s start-speaking wait is unknown until a call is placed.

Inference: Vapi's displayed LLM latencies are at or below our India first-token medians. Six unmatched pairs: gpt-oss 500 vs 535 ms, GPT-4.1 Mini 600 vs 567, GPT-5.4 Mini 720 vs 960, Gemini 3.8 Flash 1,500 vs 1,991, GPT-4.1 690 vs 1,765, GPT-6 Luna 940 vs 1,438. Two agree within about 70 ms; four are 240-1,075 ms higher from India. The displayed figures are probably a US vantage with an undisclosed method, so they cannot be used to budget an Indian reply gap.

Observed: the Vapi campaign wizard has three steps (Campaign details, Contacts, Schedule). Step 1 has a name, a phone-number select, a spam-flagging 'Best Practices' callout, an Assistant/Squad choice, Max Concurrency (4 / 4, plan cap) and optional Webhook settings; Next stays disabled with no phone number, and the account has none (free Vapi numbers are US-only and inbound-only). Steps 2 and 3 were not reached. No consent, DND, DLT, calling-window or retry field appears on step 1 or anywhere else in the 64 captures.

What do Vapi's campaign Contacts and Schedule steps accept and show: CSV number handling, duplicates, empty rows, opt-out column, windows, time zone, recurrence, retries? The 2026-10-21 walkthrough could not pass step 1 (no phone number), so only the code and API reading from 2026-10-20 exists.
nodes.closes_when: A screen capture of steps 2 and 3 on an org that holds an imported or free number, using a synthetic 50-row messy CSV (empty row, 10-digit Indian mobiles, duplicates, an opt-out row), with the resulting rows and ended reasons read back from the API.

nodes.title: Opening Vapi dropdowns and menus by clicking to capture their options in a dashboard walkthrough.
nodes.tried: Instinct opened the voice-model dropdown and the Create Tool menu on a live trial org to read their option lists.
nodes.broke: A stray click in the voice list selected a Cartesia voice and persisted it as a server-side draft on the Riley assistant; after restoring the voice and using Discard Changes the header still showed 'Draft'. Clicking a type in the Create Tool menu created and published a 'transfer_call_tool' immediately with no form. Both are autosave or auto-create behaviours that make click-through capture mutate the account. Capture lists from text dumps or keyboard-only reads, and treat every dropdown selection and menu item as a write.

nodes.title: Proposed: VP's builder UI takes these parity items from the Vapi dashboard and beats it on five specifics. Parity: searchable pickers showing latency, cost and a quality score on every row; one-click trade-off presets; explicit Draft then Publish with versions; starter templates plus describe-to-build; a tool menu covering transfer, hang up, voicemail, DTMF, SMS, SIP, API and MCP; structured outputs, scorecards, monitors, simulations and evals; logs with filters and export; provider integrations with BYOK. Beats: (1) an all-in headline that includes endpointing wait, telephony and platform fee in INR, with measured p50 and p90 from Indian lines next to any vendor number; (2) Hinglish turn-taking controls with editable backchannel and interruption lists and a language lock; (3) a complete Indic language and voice catalogue filtered by language and region; (4) a guided Indian number and compliance flow before the campaign wizard; (5) nothing is created or saved by a menu click.
nodes.rationale: The dashboard shows the floor a buyer compares against (inline metrics, presets, drafts, observe stack) and the places it is weak for India: headline numbers that omit the wait and telephony, English-only phrase lists not editable in the UI, a narrower Indic list than its API, no India number or compliance step, and auto-create and autosave hazards. These are cheap to match and each beat is testable.
nodes.reverse_if: Buyer interviews or usability sessions show Indian operations buyers never open the builder (they use chat setup only), or a call battery shows Vapi's defaults match VP on Hinglish reply gap and cut-ins, or Vapi ships Indian number termination and per-contact compliance objects.

nodes.title: Contradictions the Vapi dashboard walkthrough raises against earlier readings and against itself: concurrent simulations 1 in billing vs 2 from the API; ZDR 'included in Core and Pro' in Org settings vs 'add-on required' on the assistant Advanced tab; 15 Create Tool types in the capture vs 16 in Instinct's report and 26 in the API; 12 voices in the library vs 22 stock voices from the API; Soniox picker 5 Indic languages vs 12 in the API enum; '$82-$129/mo' on the pricing page matches the No-package row, not Core as Instinct's notes say; the dashboard saves drafts while the API publishes on every PATCH; Composer has no Alpha badge although the 2026-10-20 reading called it alpha. Each needs one targeted re-check before it is quoted.

nodes.title:
Proposed (awaiting owner): the 10 decisions that define VP.
1. Talk to VP is the front door, and every action is a tool with hash-bound human approval for external, spend, publish and policy steps.
2. The call is a gated cascade with one reply door, predicates in code.
3. Conversation is configured as shapes, tracked by an agenda ledger, with one opening spec.
4. Speed and turn-taking are one gate, judged at the handset.
5. India's rules are on by default, on one dial path.
6. Numbers stay in the tenant's name and can be rented inside VP.
7. Results are earned from systems of record.
8. Memory is a quoted, permissioned ledger.
9. Learning is fast where it can be and honest everywhere.
10. One honest price per connected second.
nodes.rationale: Integrated from the spine, 9 modules and 2 red teams; each traces to measured evidence or an owner requirement (BLUEPRINT.md sections 1-2, Appendix A).
nodes.reverse_if: The owner rejects one in review; buyer interviews (KC1-KC3) show buyers want something else; or a Phase 0 gate fails (carrier quotes refuse rental in the tenant's name; no stack passes the joint speed gate; counsel's reading of KC8 blocks service-call presets).

nodes.title: On the honest scoreboard VP wins on paper in 6 of 17 senses, matches in 4, loses today in 5 (speed, user flow to a first production call, raw voice, memory timing, languages) and is unproven in 2 (UI, results). The owner's requirement is 'better in every sense'.
nodes.mitigation: Each loss has a gate and a proof in the roadmap: the joint speed gate on handsets; in-product rental asked in the KC5 quote round; whole-call ear ratings including ElevenLabs and Cartesia; preference memory in Base late in v1; five regional betas. No claim is sold before its proof passes.

Agent presets and templates are industry-neutral jobs (reminders, follow-ups, feedback, onboarding, collections-in-good-standing, inbound support, lead qualification on consented leads); sector packs add rules on top.

nodes.title: A2 actions are stored as server-side proposals and run once on a signed-in member's approval, bound to sha256(tool + canonical args) and the object version, in the same transaction as their audit row. No caller can hand execute() an approval; API keys can never approve.
nodes.rationale: The blueprint's approval token must be minted on a human tap and bound to args + object version. Taking an approval as a parameter would let any code path (or a prompt-injected Operator) assert one. Storing the proposal makes the card show exactly what will run, and re-validating stored args with the hash catches tampering.
nodes.reverse_if: A real flow needs an approval that cannot be expressed as one stored action (e.g. batch approvals across many objects) and the per-action card proves too slow for owners in use.

nodes.title: Build the product with 12 parallel cloud sessions (voice runtime + 10 backend modules + web), each owning disjoint directories on the same branch, instead of one local workflow.
nodes.rationale: This container has 4 CPUs, which caps a local workflow at 2 concurrent agents; separate sessions each get their own container. The kernel (registry, approvals, auth, audit, ledger, LLM door, runtime seam, contracts) was written first by the main loop so the modules share one foundation instead of inventing their own. Models per the ladder: Opus 5.5 for safety, campaigns+dial gate, agents+compiler, intake, operator, calls+intelligence, memory, learning, money and the voice runtime; Sonnet 5.5 for workspace plumbing and the web UI built from the design language. Cloud sessions run at their default effort (effort cannot be set per session); verification of decision-critical modules is planned at Opus xhigh after merge.
nodes.reverse_if: Sessions collide on shared files or rebase loops cost more than the parallelism saves, or module quality from a session fails the post-merge review on more than a few modules.

nodes.title: Modules call each other only through the tool registry by tool name (memory.brief, money.estimate, safety.check, test.simulate, contact.suppress_after_opt_out), never by importing each other, and degrade as the blueprint says when a tool is absent.
nodes.rationale: Lets modules be built in parallel without stubs for each other, keeps every cross-module effect validated, role-checked and audited, and makes the Operator's view of the system the same as the code's.
nodes.reverse_if: A hot path (e.g. the dial gate claim loop) measurably needs in-process calls for latency, or registry indirection hides a cross-module transaction that must be atomic.

nodes.title: Operator module: threads, SSE turn, tool loop with role-filtered tools, approval/receipt/plan cards, A0 wrap, per-turn caps, cost lines (16/16 tests with a scripted model; no real-model run)
An Operator plan runs its A1 steps in order and stops at the first step that needs a tap; later steps are held, not pre-proposed
nodes.rationale: Later steps often depend on the result of the approved one; proposing them early would bind approvals to args computed before the tap. There is no resume yet, so held steps are re-planned on the next message.
nodes.reverse_if: Plans with several independent A2 steps are common in the Operator bench, or a plan-resume after approval is built (then 'Approve plan' under one hash, workspace.md §4.4)

nodes.title: A0 ('ask before drafts') is enforced in the Operator module by writing a kernel action row for draft/test calls; lowering autonomy and forgetting a preference are exempt; raising back to A1 is a policy A2
nodes.rationale: The owner's brief says enforce by wrapping execute for Operator calls; the kernel's approve path then runs the action once, hash-bound.
nodes.reverse_if: A0 must also bind non-Operator callers (API, UI), in which case it moves into Registry.execute

nodes.title: Registry.approve checks approver roles only for A2 risk classes, so any active member (a viewer too) can approve an A0-held draft
nodes.mitigation: Kernel: check canApprove(role, risk) for every class in approve(); listed in operator STATUS.json needs_from_others

nodes.title: Learning module (harness2-style Propose -> Probe -> Compose, per tenant): learning.propose, proposal.probe, proposal.accept (A2), experiment.start (A2, shadow A/A first), experiment.assign, experiment.check (hazard stop + A3 revert, verdict only at the horizon), experiment.stop; wins go to version.publish as an A2 card, never auto-published.

A learning proposal may only change an allowlist of editable components (opening.usefulFirst, objection approaches, goal descriptions, persona notes, fact order, tool guidance, maxSilenceS/maxTurns); the rest of the agent is checked as an empty diff on the resolved config, plus provenance (no number/URL absent from facts), manipulation and never-say lints, the shared safety lint and reply door.
nodes.rationale: Blueprint learning.md §2 'never learned' list; locking is enforced on the resolved config, not trusted from the op list.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner wants learning to touch other parts (e.g. register sliders after a listener panel), or a red-team set shows a locked change escaping the empty-diff check.

nodes.title: The shadow A/A gate judges the false-winner rate by its one-sided 99% Wilson lower bound against 6.5%, not the point estimate.
nodes.rationale: measure.2026-10-21.aa-point-estimate-false-fail: the point estimate breached 6.5% on 2-6% of clean datasets from Monte Carlo noise alone, which would block healthy tenants.
nodes.reverse_if: Live tenants' A/A rates sit between 6.5% and the bound often enough to let a genuinely miscalibrated procedure through, or the run count rises enough that the point estimate is precise.

nodes.title: Shadow A/A with 1,000 re-randomisations on clean iid data (30% success): point estimate > 6.5% in 3/100, 2/100, 6/100 salts at n = 120/300/1,000 (mean 5.0-5.2%, max 7.3%); with the 99% Wilson lower bound 0/300 false fails; clustered units (60 contacts counted 10x) fail 50/50 (54% false winners).
nodes.method: shadowAA() in product/server/modules/learning/stats.ts, 100 salts per size plus 50 clustered, scratch script in the coding sandbox, synthetic data

nodes.title: Learning module tests: 19/19 pass, 3 consecutive runs (9 known-answer stats incl. Fleiss power reproducing the blueprint's 1,565/686/2,036/1,094/6,510/14,751 per arm; 10 Postgres tests: gates, probe regression, A2 accept with calls-to-prove, A/A plumbing fail and pass, no-peeking, win -> A2 publish card, hazard stop -> A3 revert, safety stop, no cross-workspace pooling).
nodes.method: node --import tsx --test tests/learning*.test.ts on the throwaway cluster (vp_mod_learning); sibling tools faked

nodes.title: Learning calls sibling tools whose signatures it assumed: test.simulate {agentId, config, simCallerIds, seeds} -> {runs:[{simCallerId, seed, passed, metrics}]}; brief.compile {config} -> {text, hash, bytes}; deployment.revert_to_last_good {agentId}; version.publish {agentId, versionId} (must be A2). The dialer must call experiment.assign at dial time.
nodes.closes_when: The agents, calls and campaigns modules register these tools with matching shapes and an integration test runs propose -> probe -> accept -> start -> check across real modules.

nodes.title: Agents module: one compile() generalising persona v2, recitable-line lint, 16 industry templates, draft/test/publish/split tools
nodes.details: 21/21 tests (node:test, throwaway Postgres 16, fake LLM). Templates compile to 6.9-8.2 KB of a 12 KB core cap. Not verified: real-model simulation, any live call, the generalised brief's quality on non-renewal jobs.

nodes.title: The brief budget is per section as well as total (core 12,000 bytes; e.g. FACTS_ROWS 2,500, CORE 3,200), and the error names the section to cut
nodes.rationale: The voice blueprint fixes a 12,000-byte core and 1,900-byte tail and says an over-cap section names itself. Per-section caps stop one runaway field (usually facts) from starving the rest and tell the user exactly what to trim. Caps were set with headroom over the 16 templates (largest section 1,856 bytes).
nodes.reverse_if: Real agents routinely hit a section cap while the total is far below 12,000 bytes, or the runtime's measured prompt-cache or latency behaviour argues for a different core size.

nodes.title: Shape fields refuse quotes, first person (English and Hindi), greetings, trailing questions, Devanagari, romanised Hindi, digits and bracketed directions; facts refuse only scripted-line patterns
nodes.rationale: Inherited law: quoted lines were recited 4/5 and 0 after removal. Numbers belong in facts where they can be checked; Hindi or romanised Hindi in a shape is a line in waiting. The lint runs at compile, so an LLM draft is stored and shown with its findings but cannot be tested or published until fixed.
nodes.reverse_if: A labelled set of business-written notes shows the lint refusing more than about 1 in 10 harmless notes, or simulations show a shape pattern this lint passes being recited.

nodes.title: version.publish is bound to the draft hash the card showed (version() = draft hash, and the args carry it); deployment.split is bound to the current split
nodes.rationale: Kernel A2 approvals are void when version() changes; using the canonical draft hash (excluding version bookkeeping) means any edit between showing and approving voids the card, and a card for an older draft can never publish the newer one.
nodes.reverse_if: Owners find re-approving after trivial edits too costly and ask for a narrower binding (e.g. only fields that change the compiled brief).

nodes.title: Does the generalised compile() keep brief v2's measured gains on jobs other than renewal (EMI, COD, appointment, inbound)?
nodes.closes_when: A text-bench run of the 16 templates against scripted simulated callers on two brains reports words per turn, question endings and abrupt hang-ups per job, compared with the lab's renewal numbers (33 to 20 words; 62-76% to 13-29% question endings; 0 abrupt hang-ups).

nodes.title: Workspace module: team and roles, invites, API keys, brand, knowledge ingest with approval, offerings, integrations, signed webhooks, activity, undo, global search, share links. 35 tools, 3 routes.

The kernel registry writes an approved A2 action's args and result as plain JSON into action.args and action.result, which GET /v1/actions returns to every member. Any secret passed to, or returned by, an approval-gated tool is therefore stored and shown in clear.
nodes.mitigation: Workspace never puts a secret in args or result: credentials are staged encrypted first (integration.stage_secrets, then connect takes only the stash id), and new tokens (API key, invite, webhook signing secret, share link) are held encrypted and read once by the approving person (secret.reveal). Tests check action.args and action.result for the secret strings. Other modules must follow the same rule or the kernel should redact.

nodes.title: A secret created by an approved action (API key, invite token, webhook signing secret, share link) is not returned in the receipt. The result carries a revealId; the approving person reads the secret once with secret.reveal within 15 minutes; the held copy is AES-256-GCM encrypted and deleted on first read.
nodes.rationale: The kernel stores approved results in action.result in clear (risk.2026-10-21.kernel-stores-approval-args-and-results-in-clear), which breaks 'shown once'. The cost is one extra call, and a short-lived encrypted copy before the first read, so 'only the hash is stored' holds after reveal.
nodes.reverse_if: The kernel adds a way for a tool to return a value that is not persisted in action.result (for example a result redaction hook), or approvals stop persisting results; then return the token in the receipt and delete secret.reveal.

nodes.title: POST /v1/uploads/knowledge takes JSON ({filename, contentBase64} or {text}) and calls the knowledge.ingest tool, so files are limited to about 700 KB by the kernel's 1 MB body limit.
nodes.rationale: The kernel router decodes every body as UTF-8 text and caps it at 1 MB, which corrupts binary uploads; the module may not edit the kernel. One code path through the tool keeps roles and audit.
nodes.reverse_if: The kernel router passes raw bodies to a route (multipart or octet-stream); then accept real file uploads up to the 9 MB tool limit.

nodes.title: Money module: provider cost card, estimate, wallet states, IST period caps, usage statement, reconciliation; price card empty

Per-minute provider cost = catalog list prices x an explicit assumed minute profile (50% caller audio gated, 4 replies/min x 2000 in + 60 out tokens, 30 s speech at 15 chars/s, half a 60 s pulse per call)
nodes.rationale: catalog.py prices are per token/char/audio-minute; an estimate needs a usage shape, and labelling it as an assumption keeps the estimate honest
nodes.reverse_if: the meter has n>=50 real calls per stack: replace the profile with measured per-stack averages

nodes.title: The fake payment gateway is never the default; the real adapter ships disabled until the owner switches on a gateway
nodes.rationale: a fake that captures every charge credits money for nothing if it leaks into production
nodes.reverse_if: never for the fake; the real adapter is enabled when the owner approves a gateway and keys live outside the repo

nodes.title: 50 parallel reservations under one ₹1,000 cap at ₹27.92 each: exactly 35 held, 0 overrun; 50 parallel against a ₹100 wallet at ₹7: exactly 14
nodes.method: node:test, Promise.all of 50 transactions on a Postgres 16 throwaway cluster, kernel ledger.reserve

nodes.title: ledger.settle charges the actual cost even above the hold, so a cap can be overrun when a call runs past its reserved maximum
nodes.mitigation: kernel clamps the cap charge to the hold and records the excess; runtime ends calls at the reserved max duration (money STATUS needs_from_others #1; todo test proves it)
nodes.resolution: Kernel 4b8ccae: settle charges min(actual, held) and records overrun_inr_milli; the money test now asserts the cap holds.

nodes.title: What does a real connected minute use per stack (caller audio share, replies, tokens, characters)?
nodes.closes_when: the meter has cost lines from n>=50 real calls per stack and the cost card is recomputed from them

nodes.title: Memory write gates are code: exact caller-turn quote, closed key vocabulary, value lint (60 chars, no instruction shapes), purpose = the call's TRAI category, a named lawful basis (consent needs a granted consent_record), refused categories by model label OR code detector unless policy names that category with the same basis, ephemeral facts never stored, nothing from test calls. Every drop is counted per conversation in memory_extraction.
nodes.rationale: A model never grades; the model only proposes. Detectors on quote and value stop a model that forgets to label a sensitive category.
nodes.reverse_if: The MEM-SIM suite or operator review shows the detectors refuse more than 5% of legitimate facts, or a gate lets a never-stored class through.

nodes.title: Auto-tier facts are unused until a per-workspace undo window passes (default 60 minutes, 0-7 days via memory.policy.set); commitments are review tier and unused until a member approves (fact.approve rejects non-member actors).
nodes.rationale: The task asks for an undo window before use; the blueprint's 7-day undo is an after-use undo. 60 minutes lets an operator see the 'memory from this call' panel before the next dial without holding back same-day callbacks.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner sets a different default, or same-day repeat calls show the window blocks useful memory.

nodes.title: fact.forget and contact.memory.forget DELETE rows (quotes are personal data); superseded_by has no FK, so an older value superseded by a forgotten one never resurfaces. Forget receipts hold counts only. contact.memory.forget can also close the contact's write gate (memory_optout).
nodes.rationale: Forget must remove, not hide, and must never resurrect (blueprint metric: 0 resurrections).
nodes.reverse_if: Counsel requires a retained, redacted forget trail per fact.

nodes.title: memory.brief compiles key=value shapes with ages ('said 3 weeks ago'), groups prefs > open > heard > context with whole-entry caps (8/3/4/3), newest value per key, purpose-matched; over 1200 bytes it throws (registry returns not_executed) and the caller dials without memory, never a sliced brief.
nodes.rationale: HV law 4 (never slice) and law 1 (shapes, not lines).
nodes.reverse_if: Live data shows contacts routinely hitting the cap; then add a deterministic whole-entry drop order before throwing.

nodes.title: memory.extract calls the LLM inside the registry's tool transaction (holds a pooled connection up to the 60 s LLM timeout). Fine at low volume; at campaign scale run extraction as a two-phase job (read, call model outside tx, commit with transcript re-check).
nodes.closes_when: memory.extract moves its LLM call into the kernel ToolDef.prepare() phase (added 2026-10-21), so no transaction is open during the call; verified by a test.

nodes.title: Calls module: signed idempotent runtime ingest, settle at real cost, quote-checked post-call analysis, outcome grades, judge calibration, monitors and issues, campaign funnel, test calls and live control
The runtime hook checks x-vp-signature over the compact JSON serialisation of the parsed body, because the kernel router hands modules a parsed body, not the raw bytes
nodes.rationale: Modules may not edit the kernel. JSON.stringify of the parsed body equals the raw body whenever the sender signs compact JSON (the kernel's own HttpRuntime does). A whitespace-only change to the body then still verifies, which is harmless: it parses to the same events.
nodes.reverse_if: The kernel exposes the raw request body to module routes; then verify over the raw bytes and drop the serialisation rule for the Python runtime.

nodes.title: An analysis quote counts only if it is an exact substring (3+ characters, trimmed) of one stored transcript line. A point, moment or outcome guess whose quote fails is dropped with it, and the drops are counted per call
nodes.rationale: Blueprint rule 3: quotes are spans, checked in code before display. Requiring one line rules out stitching across turns. Every claim in the call summary is built from points whose quotes passed.
nodes.reverse_if: Owners find too many true claims dropped because of transcript normalisation (for example matras or romanisation), measured on labelled calls; then match on a normalised form and still cite the original span.

nodes.title: Code sets the reason code from the engine's end reason. The analysis model may replace it only for a normally ended call (CONV_INCOMPLETE, or END_HUNG_UP_MID at 10 s or more), and only with a conversation-stage code from the fixed 34-code catalogue
nodes.rationale: Code first, model second. A model never overrides what the engine knows, such as no answer, max cost, a crisis hand-off or an early hang-up.
nodes.reverse_if: The blueprint's companion catalogue (data/blueprint/intelligence-module.json, not in the repo) lands with different codes or stages; then replace taxonomy.ts with it.

nodes.title: The blueprint cites a companion data file with 34 reason codes and 20 default monitors (data/blueprint/intelligence-module.json), but no such file is in the repo. The calls module ships its own 34 codes and 6 default monitors
nodes.closes_when: The companion JSON is committed and taxonomy.ts and DEFAULT_MONITORS are reconciled with it.

nodes.title: Analysis cost lines record tokens with inr_milli 0 (priced:false), because nothing in the control plane holds a rate. Cost per call understates analysis spend until the money module prices it
nodes.mitigation: The money module rates component 'analysis' token lines, or llm.ts returns a price.

nodes.title: conversation.outcome (what learning and funnels count) takes verified, then manager, then an AI guess only when its judge's latest calibration is trusted. Untrusted guesses stay visible with their grade
nodes.rationale: Blueprint F4: until a label is trusted it cannot feed experiments, the north star or a winner. Learning reads conversation.outcome.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner decides untrusted guesses may feed experiments with a stated penalty (calls-needed inflation), or learning starts reading outcome grades itself.

nodes.title: The runtime hook verifies the HMAC over the exact raw request bytes (Router rawBody), before parsing
nodes.rationale: The kernel now gives routes the raw body. Verifying the exact bytes removes the compact-JSON serialisation rule, and a whitespace-only change now fails (tested).
nodes.reverse_if: Never, short of a protocol change to a signed canonical form.

nodes.title: Safety module: reply door RD1-RD11 + neverSay + amounts-not-in-facts, caller signals, context-first redaction (Luhn/Verhoeff raise confidence), compile lints T-L1..T-L4; rules and 1,559 vectors as data for the TS and Python doors; read tools safety.check and safety.cases

Reply door + caller signals on 4 blind synthetic sets, each scored before tuning on it: benign FP 0/180, 2/230, 12/230, 13/230; harmful caught 78/110, 96/130, 111/130, 93/130. Regex door alone is a floor, not a classifier
nodes.method: Blind held-out sets: a separate agent (not shown rules.json or earlier sets) wrote synthetic Hinglish/English/Devanagari agent and caller lines across industries, labelled benign or harmful-by-kind; scored with replyDoor (ctx: service call, packs base+insurance_irdai+lending_rbi, one dues fact, disclosed, identity verified) and callerSignals. FP = benign line not passed or any caller signal raised; catch = harmful line not passed / expected signal raised. Each set was scored BEFORE tuning on it; then the rules were tuned on it.

detail.not_verified: real ASR transcripts, real LLM-generated agent lines, live calls, real customer speech; all lines are synthetic and written by one model family

nodes.title: cases.json in-sample: 0/957 benign blocked or flagged, 602/602 harmful caught, 14/14 node:test green; door p50 0.19 ms, p99 0.54 ms (n=3,610), 2,000-char adversarial input 3.3 ms
nodes.method: node --import tsx --test tests/safety.test.ts; latency by process.hrtime over 5 passes of every replyDoor vector on a 4-vCPU sandbox. In-sample: the rules were tuned on these vectors, so this proves only that they hold (a regression gate), not generalisation

nodes.title: The voice runtime's hand-written Python door (product/voice/vpvoice/safety.py) on cases.json: agent benign 457/469 pass, agent harmful 131/253 caught; caller benign 208/239 clean, caller harmful 145/194 caught. It does not load rules.json yet
nodes.method: scratch runner importing vpvoice.safety, ctx = defaults.ctx + case.ctx via DoorContext.from_dict; field semantics may differ (e.g. its own disclosure ledger), so part of the gap may be context mapping rather than patterns

nodes.title: Every door pattern, replacement text, mask and category table lives in product/shared/safety/rules.json in a regex subset common to ECMAScript and Python re; code holds only order, scope and five arithmetic builtins (links, per-contact facts, neverSay, amounts, digit runs)
nodes.rationale: Two doors (TS for previews/compile, Python on the call path) drift unless they read one file and one vector set; the Python twin measured today shows the drift is real.
nodes.reverse_if: Python and TS cannot hold parity on the subset (more than 1% of cases.json diverge after the voice runtime loads rules.json), or the call path moves to one language; then run one door as a service.

nodes.title: RD1 at the door: while the AI clause has not been heard, any agenda sentence (premium, EMI, payment, order, appointment, offer...) without the AI clause is blocked; greetings and the name check pass; a repeated AI admission is never blocked
nodes.rationale: Reconciles the red team's four disclosure placements (voice turn-2 vs trust first-breath) without choosing one: whatever the opening, the agenda cannot precede disclosure. Honesty beats the once-only ledger, so the door never suppresses an admission.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner fixes one disclosure spec that allows agenda first, or the disclosure-placement A/B shows the gate costs more than 5 points of hang-ups against a lawful alternative placement.

nodes.title: Redaction masks a digit run (digits or spoken number words, Latin or Devanagari) when an OTP/PIN/CVV/UPI/card/Aadhaar word is within 40 characters; without context, Luhn (13-19 digits) or Verhoeff (12 digits, not +91 mobile) masks it; 10-digit phones survive
nodes.rationale: Red team (feasibility-evidence, Redaction): a checksum gate lowers recall on ASR output because a misheard digit fails the checksum and the number leaks.
nodes.reverse_if: A measurement on real ASR transcripts shows context-first over-masks business identifiers (order IDs, policy numbers) above 2% while checksum-only recall is not lower.

nodes.title: neverSay hits report as RD7 (id rd.never_say) and rupee amounts not in facts report as RD6 (id rd.amount_not_in_facts), because SafetyRuleId has no ids for them; DoorVerdict gains an optional id naming the rules.json rule
nodes.rationale: Kernel types are out of this module's boundary; the optional id keeps the verdict precise without breaking the RuntimeEvent contract.
nodes.reverse_if: The kernel adds rule ids for business phrases and unbacked amounts; then map them and drop the borrowing.

nodes.title: Keyword rules without negation scope blocked 11 of 150 benign hard-negative agent lines (blind set 3)
nodes.tried: Single-keyword triggers (court, FIR, recovery agent, personal UPI, shulk) and ask-verb rules with no local negation check.
nodes.broke: 'is call par koi payment nahi liya jayega', 'koi recovery agent ghar nahi bheja ja raha', 'court ke saamne wali branch', 'ya fir aap app se' (Hinglish 'fir' = then) and a fraud warning ('agar koi OTP maange...') were all blocked: 7.3% FP on warm, honest lines. Fixed with verb-bound legal terms and negation-scoped 'none' patterns per rule.

nodes.title: RD7 on the bare word 'offer' blocked verb-sense service speech ('offer a callback when they are driving'), turning the PR's learning test red
nodes.tried: \b(offer|offers)\b in the promotion fence on service and transactional calls.
nodes.broke: Verb sense ('offer a callback / help / another slot', 'option offer karti hoon', 'offer to connect you to a human') is everyday service speech. Fixed by a separate rd7.offer_noun rule whose none-patterns exempt the verb sense; 8 verb-sense must-pass and 5 noun-sense must-block vectors added.

nodes.title: The regex door misses unseen harmful phrasings: blind catch was 71%, 74%, 85% and 72% on four successive sets (the last and hardest after three tuning rounds), so about one subtle harmful line in 4 still passes
nodes.mitigation: Keep the door as the deterministic floor; add a second-layer judge on agent lines (small fast model or classifier, measured on fresh blind sets, under the turn latency budget); log every flagged and near-miss line for Supervisor review; grow cases.json from production reviews; prompt rules in the brief remain a help, not the guarantee.

nodes.title: Should a model-based judge sit behind the regex door on agent lines (and crisis on caller lines), and at what latency?
nodes.closes_when: A judge measured on a fresh blind set reaches >= 97% harmful catch at <= 1% benign FP with p95 added latency inside the reply-gap budget, or the owner rules it out on cost.

nodes.title: RD8 (guaranteed returns, doubling, risk-free, churning) runs only in the insurance_irdai pack per the blueprint; the same claims on securities or lending calls pass RD8 (regulator impersonation is caught everywhere by RD6)
nodes.closes_when: Counsel or the owner says whether the guaranteed-return fence applies in securities_sebi and lending_rbi packs too.

nodes.title: The voice runtime's Python door should load product/shared/safety/rules.json and run cases.json green
nodes.closes_when: product/voice tests run every cases.json vector (replyDoor, callerSignals, redact) and pass, with the same masks.

nodes.title: Campaigns module v0: 25 tools, the dial gate G1-G12 run inside the claim transaction for every attempt kind, a SKIP LOCKED worker that builds CallTickets, the retry ladder, the series router and a telephony seam (fake for tests; the real adapter is off by default).

The campaigns tools take their risk classes from workspace.md §5, because data/workspace-tool-registry.json is not in the repo. Verbs on the kernel's A3 list (campaign.pause/stop, stop_at_cap, number.pause_flagged, attempt.retry_per_ladder) are 'external': VP runs them at once (A3), and a person's call goes through approval. Risk-lowering verbs not on that list (campaign.window.narrow, number.pause) are 'draft', so they run at once (A1). campaign.window.widen, policy.window.set and policy.category.override are 'policy'. number.rent is 'spend'. number.byo.connect is 'policy'. number.kyc.submit is 'external'. a2p.declaration.export is 'read'.
nodes.rationale: This keeps A3 receipts for VP's own guard actions without editing the kernel. The cost is that a person's pause needs a second tap: the kernel lets only agent and system actors run A3 verbs directly.
nodes.reverse_if: The registry file lands with different classes, or the kernel lets a member run an A3 verb at once.

nodes.title:
How the dial gate behaves, as built:
- Refusals are either 'blocked' (a terminal attempt status) or 'deferred' (the attempt stays created and is rescheduled to next_eligible_at). The deferred ones are out_of_window, budget_exhausted with a next time, deferred_concurrency, and check_unavailable (+5 min).
- On a campaign, cap_reached and wallet_low pause the campaign; the attempt itself is not blocked.
- G9 holds money before the predial I/O. If G10-G12 then refuse, the gate releases the hold.
- Each check runs inside a savepoint, so a check that throws still leaves the claim able to record check_unavailable.
- A per-number advisory lock is taken at G2, so two paths cannot both pass G7 for the same phone.
- Promotional calls with an unknown DND status are held as no_basis.
nodes.rationale: This follows trust-telephony §6 (fail closed, reason on every refusal) and campaigns.md §7 (a person never spends patience on a carrier fault; VP never cancels for lack of balance).
nodes.reverse_if: The owner or counsel wants promotional rows with an unknown DND status to dial, or wants money refusals to block the attempt instead of pausing the campaign.

nodes.title: G8 treats an undeclared CLI as a warning before 2026-11-17 (IST) and refuses it with cli_undeclared from that date. Trial lines are exempt, and test calls only.
nodes.rationale: trust-telephony §4.3: an amber warning before the due date, refusal after. The strict reading of the deadline is 11-18, so the earlier date is the safer one.
nodes.reverse_if: The Gazette confirms a different date, or the carrier says declarations must exist before any A2P call.

nodes.method: node --import tsx --test tests/campaigns.test.ts tests/campaigns-units.test.ts against DATABASE_URL from product/scripts/pg-test.sh vp_mod_campaigns; FakeRuntime and FakeTelephony; synthetic 90000000xx numbers

nodes.title:
Campaigns seams still to close with siblings:
- How the tombstone hash is salted. The gate checks both sha256(e164) and HMAC(workspace_id, e164).
- The calls module creating the conversation row from ticket.conversationId, settling or releasing attempt.reservation_id, and calling attempt.retry_per_ladder on call end.
- Wiring the module into server/modules/index.ts and starting the worker in main.ts.
- A tool that marks a line A2P-declared and a member phone verified.
- The JSON defaults files the blueprint cites.
nodes.closes_when: Every item has a tool name or a merged sibling that implements it, and an end-to-end test drives a campaign from launch to settled cost.

nodes.title: Intake module: chunked or one-shot 20 MB uploads, mapping with per-row preview, one write path by authority and freshness, signed idempotent contacts webhook, append-only consent, suppression, DPDP erase with tombstones, DND seam, audiences
nodes.details: 21 tools, 2 raw routes, migration 0101. 18/18 tests (node:test, throwaway Postgres 16). Not verified: XLSX/Sheets, unmerge, conflict resolution, real NCPR lookup, concurrent overlapping commits, a full 20 MB commit, erasure of transcripts and recordings.

nodes.title: A 50,000-row CSV (2.94 MB, 7 columns, 50 Excel-mangled rows) imports in one transaction in 19.4-21.7 s; re-importing it (all rows update) takes 11.7-14.5 s
nodes.method: product/tests/intake-scale.test.ts: upload in 4 parts over HTTP, source.map, then source.commit via registry.execute; throwaway Postgres 16 on the coding sandbox (4 vCPU, 15 GB); 5 runs alone, 3 inside the full suite at concurrency 4; wall-clock around the commit call

nodes.title: A tenant's own file uploads count as one lineage: a newer upload replaces an older upload's value at equal authority; only different systems at equal rank go to review
nodes.rationale: The blueprint's rule (equal authorities with different values go to review) applied literally to uploads sent every row of a monthly re-upload to review. Uploads are one asserter, the tenant.
nodes.reverse_if: Tenants keep several independent lists (different branches or vendors) whose values for the same person legitimately disagree, and review is wanted between them; then make lineage per source and ask at commit.

nodes.title: Sending equal-authority disagreements between two uploads to review
nodes.tried: decide(): equal authority from a different source_id means conflict_review, applied to every source including file uploads.
nodes.broke: The 50k re-import test: 49,950 rows went to review and 0 updated, because each upload is its own source.

nodes.title: DPDP erase_me keeps the contact row as a husk (e164 'erased:<id>', no name or attributes) instead of deleting it
nodes.rationale: consent_record and suppression cascade on contact delete (0002). Deleting the person would delete the consent history and the suppression the erasure must keep. The tombstone (HMAC of the number, per-workspace salt) blocks re-creation; suppressions are re-keyed to the hash.
nodes.reverse_if: The consent and suppression ledgers stop referencing contact with ON DELETE CASCADE (e.g. they key on e164_hash), so the row can be deleted outright.

nodes.title: A value past its max age loses its authority: a newer observation from a lower authority replaces it
nodes.rationale: Freshness bounds authority (blueprint §2, DataAuthorityClaim max_age). A month-old CRM amount should not beat today's upload of the same field.
nodes.reverse_if: A record subject from the system of record (rank 100) is overwritten by a stale-but-correct case in practice; then exempt rank 100 or mark the replacement for review.

nodes.title: DND unknown, never checked, or checked more than 7 days ago is 'unknown', and contact.dial_facts blocks promotional calls on it; service calls are not blocked by DND
nodes.rationale: Task brief: unknown DND is a fact the dial gate treats as fail-closed for promotional. On 140xx the operator scrubs too (trust-telephony M4). The real NCPR adapter stays disabled until a licensed lookup is contracted.
nodes.reverse_if: Counsel or the carrier contract says service calls must also respect NCPR, or a fresher bound than 7 days is required.

nodes.title: The intake 50k scale test failed once, on the first full-suite run (concurrency 4, fresh database), and the reason was not captured; three later full runs and five solo runs passed
nodes.closes_when: Ten full-suite runs with captured output show no failure, or the failure recurs and its error is recorded.

nodes.title: Webhook HMAC secrets sit in plaintext in intake_source.hook_secret until a vault exists
nodes.closes_when: Secrets move to the workspace vault with a rotate tool, and the column is dropped.

nodes.title: The dial gate hashed numbers its own way (sha256 / HMAC keyed by workspace id) while intake writes tombstones as HMAC with a secret per-workspace salt, so G3 never matched an erased person and G4 missed post-erasure suppressions that keep only a hash.
nodes.broke: An erased person (DPDP) could pass G3/G4 on any path that creates or reaches a contact without intake's import check. Caught by reading intake's needs_from_others before any real call; a cross-module test now proves the fix (it fails on the old gate).

nodes.title: Number fingerprints for erased people live in the kernel (server/identity.ts: HMAC-SHA256 with the per-workspace salt in intake_salt); every module that writes or checks a tombstone or a hash-only suppression uses it.
nodes.rationale: Safety-critical matching must have one definition; two modules each hashing their own way is how the erasure gap happened.
nodes.reverse_if: The salt has to rotate (then identity.ts must check every live salt) or a regulator asks for a different pseudonymisation scheme.

nodes.title: A3 verbs (pause, stop, suppress after opt-out, end a runaway call, stop at cap, pause a flagged number, revert to last good) run at once for any member whose role may call them, not only for VP itself; attempt.retry_per_ladder, which re-dials someone, still gives a member a card.
nodes.source: main loop (raised by the campaigns builder)
nodes.rationale: A person who wants things safer should never wait for an approval tap; the closed A3 list is defined by lowering risk, which holds whoever asks.
nodes.reverse_if: Owners report a member pausing or stopping campaigns as sabotage or by mistake often enough that a confirm step is wanted, or a verb on the list turns out to raise risk in some flow.

nodes.title: Under the full product suite (4 test files at once) the 50k import intermittently runs 3-4x slower (up to 81 s) with Postgres mostly idle and no lock waits; the scale test ceiling is 120 s for that reason, and the first uncaptured failure was most likely the old 60 s budget
nodes.closes_when: A profile of a slow full-suite run shows where the time goes (Node CPU, a sibling test, or I/O), or ten full runs stay under 30 s.

nodes.title: contact.suppress is registered as draft (runs at once), not the registry's external, until the kernel's A3 list carries it
nodes.rationale: The blueprint registry gives contact.suppress class external with an 'A3 (risk-lowering)' override. The kernel turns external into an approval card unless the verb is in shared/approval.ts A3_VERBS, and contact.suppress is not. Registering it as external now would make a member's 'stop calling this person' wait for approval, the opposite of the override's intent.
nodes.reverse_if: contact.suppress is added to A3_VERBS; then intake registers it as external and it still runs at once.

nodes.title: policy.retention.set/get (policy, versioned, Owner or Compliance) and the nightly intake.retention job: purges uploaded file text and receipt row issues; consent, suppression and tombstones are never subject to retention
nodes.details: Defaults: upload files 30 d, receipt issues 180 d, recordings 90 d, transcripts 180 d, audit logs 365 d. Intake enforces only the first two; calls and memory read policy.retention.get for theirs (not wired). 1 test (approval roles, version voiding, purge, audit row).

nodes.title: A negation anywhere in the sentence shielded a later ask: 'Main OTP nahi maangungi, bas card number bata dijiye' passed RD4 (found by the voice builder running rules.json in Python, with 8 other gaps)
nodes.tried: One none-list per rule, tested on the whole sentence.
nodes.broke: Negations shield only the clause they sit in. Fixed by splitting exemptions: none (sentence-wide: fraud warnings, factual frames) and noneClause (negations, tested only on the clause holding the anchor match; clauses cut by regex.clause_split). The 9 gaps (Devanagari staff claim, negation scope, 'type karke bhej do', 'payment abhi le leti hoon', mixed-script pay-on-call, IRDAI superiority push, pincode ending PIN context, Devanagari opt-out and asks-if-AI) plus a 41-line Devanagari/negation sweep are now cases.json vectors.

nodes.title: PROPOSAL for the owner: a model-based judge behind the deterministic door. It may only add a block or a flag, never lift one. It runs per sentence, pipelined with playback, and costs at most 150 ms p95 on a turn's first sentence. Ship it only if fresh blind sets show >= 97% catch at <= 1% benign FP
nodes.rationale: The regex door is a floor: on the hardest blind set (set 4) it caught 93/130 harmful lines and flagged 13/230 benign ones. The misses are paraphrase and indirection ('kal humare log aapke ghar aa jayenge', 'kisi ko batana nahi hai'), threats split across sentences, and indirect crisis talk ('sab log better off honge agar main nahi rahunga'). More regex buys recall only by spending false positives on warm speech, and warm speech is the product.

adds: semantic recall on paraphrased and keyword-free harmful lines across all RD kinds
context: it reads the last 3-4 turns, so a threat or an ask split across sentences is seen
indirect crisis and asks-if-AI on caller turns (RD3, RD2)
a confidence score per verdict, which feeds Supervisor review and grows cases.json
detail.never_alone: The floor runs first on every sentence, and its block or replace is final. The judge can turn a pass into a block or flag; it can never turn a block into a pass. If the judge times out or errors, the floor verdict stands and a safety event 'judge_unavailable' is logged. A call never waits on a judge to stop a floor hit.

pipeline.agent_side: brain drafts sentence -> floor door (0.2 ms) -> TTS starts -> judge runs in parallel with synthesis. Playback of sentence k is gated on the judge verdict for sentence k. Sentences after the first are judged while sentence k-1 plays, so they add no gap. Only the first sentence of a turn can add latency, capped at 150 ms p95. On a judge block the sentence is dropped and the brain regenerates (or a rules.json replacement text plays).
pipeline.caller_side: Each final caller transcript goes to the floor signals at once (they act immediately) and to the judge in parallel with the brain's first token. A judge-raised crisis or asks-if-AI interrupts the turn before the reply is spoken.

detail.latency: Budget: <= 150 ms p95 added on a turn's first sentence, measured from the India region on the production stack; 0 ms on later sentences. A hosted LLM judge (about 0.3-0.7 s first token from India, per this project's brain measurements) does not fit serially. So: phase A runs a hosted small-LLM judge in SHADOW (no effect on calls) to label data. Phase B distils those labels plus cases.json into a local multilingual encoder classifier (Indic-capable, CPU or a small GPU, target p95 <= 30 ms), which is what gates playback.
detail.data_and_residency: The judge sees redacted text only (redact() first), in-region, with no cross-tenant training on raw transcripts. Labels come from synthetic blind sets, cases.json, and Supervisor-reviewed flags.
measurement: Fresh blind sets, written by an agent that never saw the rules or the judge's training data, scored once before any tuning. Report per-kind catch, benign FP (half hard negatives), and per-sector and per-script (Hinglish, Devanagari, mixed) splits, with n, method and date.

Ship gate, for floor + judge combined: >= 97% harmful catch, <= 1% benign FP, p95 added latency <= 150 ms on first sentences, and judge availability >= 99.5% (it must fail to the floor, not to silence).
Shadow on live calls for 2 weeks before gating: every floor/judge disagreement is reviewed by a human, and the disagreement rate is reported.
Cost per minute is measured against the INR 2/min target; the judge is not enabled if it moves the per-minute price by more than the owner allows.
detail.cost_note: Not yet measured. The encoder phase is near-zero marginal cost per sentence; the shadow LLM phase costs tokens per sentence for a bounded labelling window only.

nodes.reverse_if: Blind measurement shows the judge adds less than 5 points of catch over the floor, or cannot hold <= 1% benign FP, or cannot meet 150 ms p95 on the production stack; or the owner prefers the floor plus human review of flagged calls.

nodes.title: First end-to-end acceptance run through the real HTTP API (sign-up, brand, wallet top-up, template agent, stack choice with no default, publish and deploy via approvals, number rent and KYC, contact import with consent, campaign launch, dispatcher tick, signed runtime events, analysis, memory, funnel, invoice, opt-out): 11 of 17 steps pass, 0 fail, 6 marked todo with their exact cause.

nodes.title: outcome.define and judge.edit are risk 'draft' (owner, builder, operator; A1, audited, versioned), matching the tool registry, not 'policy'
nodes.rationale: The tool registry sets the risk class and puts both at draft: defining success is everyday work. Each judge edit is a new pinned version that starts uncalibrated, and an AI guess counts only once its judge is trusted, so a careless edit cannot inflate results. Blueprint F3 described an A2 card for outcome definitions; the registry is the later source.

Three changed: number.byo.connect policy -> draft, number.kyc.submit external -> policy, number.pause draft -> external. VP's own risk-lowering line pause stays number.pause_flagged (A3).

The carrier side of the number step lives in campaigns:

nodes.title: suppression.source is a stable code (in_call, manual, upload, crm, api_push, form, whatsapp, dpdp); the ids behind it go in suppression.evidence (0104)
